definition_zh: 拉；拖；拔出；拉伤；拉力；吸引力；影响力
definition_en: to move something towards oneself or in a stated direction by using force; to remove something by drawing it out; to injure a muscle; also the force that draws, a physical attraction, and personal influence
core_image: 一个人双手攥住粗绳，脚蹬地面，把绳子一点点拽向自己
scene: 绳子另一头卡在石缝里，几个人排成一列，脚掌抵住地面，一起把劲儿往后使。They pulled the rope until the log slid out of the mud.
sceneCN: 这里 pull 是「拉、拽」（第 1 个义项：用力把东西朝自己或某个方向移动）；句意为他们一直拉绳子，直到那根木头从泥里滑出来。图中可辨识物件：粗绳、石缝、蹬地的脚。

pos.zh: 拉；拖；拔出；拉伤
拉力；吸引力；影响力

derivatives.zh: pull 与 over 复合，指从头上套下去穿的毛衣
pull 与 back 复合，指军队或企业的撤退、收缩
pull 加表人后缀 -er，指拉东西的人或拔取工具

senses.title: To move something towards oneself
senses.definition: to move a person or thing towards oneself or along behind oneself by using force
senses.definitionCN: 用力把人或物朝自己方向移动，或让其在身后跟着移动
senses.example: She pulled the heavy box across the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那个沉重的箱子拖着在地板上移动。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to pluck or tug at something, so the body's grip and the backward motion are both built into the word from the start.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词本义是「揪、拽」，所以手握住的力道和向后移动的方向从一开始就长在词里。

senses.title: To remove something by drawing it out
senses.definition: to take something out of a place or a body by drawing it steadily away
senses.definitionCN: 通过持续往外拽，把某物从某个位置或身体里取出来
senses.example: The dentist pulled two of his teeth.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医拔掉了他两颗牙。
senses.why: Pulling in the first sense moves a whole object; aim the same motion at a part held inside something and the meaning narrows to extraction.
senses.whyCN: 第一义的拉是移动整个物体；把同样的动作对准嵌在某物内部的东西，词义就收窄为「拔出」。

senses.title: To injure a muscle by overstretching it
senses.definition: to damage a muscle or tendon by stretching it too far
senses.definitionCN: 因拉伸过度而损伤肌肉或肌腱
senses.example: He pulled a muscle in his calf during the sprint.
senses.exampleCN: 他在短跑时拉伤了小腿肌肉。
senses.why: The fibres of a muscle are drawn apart by a sudden load, and English describes that damage with the same verb it uses for drawing something apart.
senses.whyCN: 肌肉纤维被突然的负荷拽开，英语就用「往开拽」这个动词来描述这种损伤。

senses.title: A steady force that draws something
senses.definition: a force that draws an object steadily in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 把物体持续朝某个方向吸引的力
senses.example: The pull of the moon lifts the sea into tides.
senses.exampleCN: 月球的引力把海水拉起，形成潮汐。
senses.why: Once the verb names the act, the noun can name the force behind it, so a rope, a magnet and the moon all exert a pull.
senses.whyCN: 动词一旦指这个动作，名词就能指动作背后的力，于是绳子、磁铁和月亮都能产生 pull。

senses.title: Personal influence or attraction
senses.definition: the power to influence events or attract people, especially through connections
senses.definitionCN: 影响事情或吸引他人的力量，尤指凭借人脉关系
senses.example: His family has a lot of pull in this town.
senses.exampleCN: 他家在这个镇上很有门路。
senses.why: A person with connections can draw decisions the way a rope draws a load, so the physical sense extends to social leverage and charm.
senses.whyCN: 有门路的人能像绳子拉动货物那样牵动决定，于是物理义延伸到社会上的影响力与魅力。

intro.en: Pull is an Old English verb of Germanic stock, first recorded as pullian with the sense of plucking or tugging; it has no reliable Latin cognate, so the Latin comparison is left empty.
intro.cn: pull 是源自日耳曼语族的古英语动词，最早写作 pullian，意为「揪、拽」；它没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁对照留空。

items.en: Pullian is recorded in Old English with the sense of plucking wool or tugging at something, and it already implies a hand closing on a thing.
items.cn: 古英语中的 pullian 意为揪羊毛、拽东西，词里已经含有「手攥住某物」的意思。

items.en: The verb belongs to the Germanic layer of English rather than to the Latin layer, and related forms appear in several Germanic languages.
items.cn: 这个动词属于英语的日耳曼语层而非拉丁语层，在几种日耳曼语言中都有相关形式。

items.en: Middle English kept the verb and widened it from plucking to any steady drawing motion, including pulling a cart or a rope.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个动词，并把词义从「揪」扩大到任何持续拖拽的动作，包括拉车、拉绳。

items.en: By the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the noun pull appears beside the verb, naming the act and later the force itself.
items.cn: 到十六、十七世纪，名词 pull 出现在动词旁边，先指拉这个动作，后来指拉力本身。

items.en: Modern English uses pull for drawing, extracting, straining a muscle, physical attraction, and social influence, and keeps it in dozens of phrasal verbs.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pull 表示拉、拔出、拉伤肌肉、物理吸引与社会影响力，并让它出现在大量短语动词中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short words that differ from pull by one sound or letter; the near-meaning group collects other verbs for moving something by force.
note.cn: 形近组收与 pull 只差一个音或一个字母的短词；近义组收其他表示「用力移动某物」的动词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a short Germanic verb for closing a hand on something and drawing it back, and its family keeps that backward motion.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个简短的日耳曼动词，指手攥住东西往后拽，它的同族词都保留着这股向后的力道。

normal.en: Pull goes back to Old English pullian, to pluck or tug, and it never needed a Latin ancestor.
normal.cn: pull 上溯到古英语 pullian（揪、拽），它从来不需要一个拉丁祖先。

normal.en: Pull out, pull up and pull over are phrasal verbs: the particle tells you which direction the drawing goes.
normal.cn: pull out、pull up、pull over 都是短语动词，小品词告诉你拉力朝哪个方向。

normal.en: Pull a muscle is the same motion turned inward, because the fibres are drawn apart inside the leg.
normal.cn: pull a muscle 是把同一个动作转向身体内部，因为腿里的纤维被拽开了。

normal.en: Pullover is a garment you pull over your head, so the compound keeps the original gesture in plain sight.
normal.cn: pullover 是从头上拉下去穿的衣服，复合词把原来的动作明明白白留在里面。

normal.en: The noun pull can mean influence, because a person who can draw decisions is doing what a rope does to a load.
normal.cn: 名词 pull 能指影响力，因为能牵动决定的人，做的正是绳子对货物做的事。

abstract.en: A pull is a relationship: something on one end always answers to something on the other.
abstract.cn: 拉是一种关系：一端的东西总是在回应另一端。

abstract.en: English lets one short verb cover rope, tooth, muscle and reputation, because all four resist and then give way.
abstract.cn: 英语让一个短动词同时覆盖绳子、牙齿、肌肉和名声，因为这四样都会先抵抗、然后松脱。

abstract.en: What draws a person is not so different from what draws a boat: a force outside, and a rope that holds.
abstract.cn: 吸引一个人的力量和拉动一条船的力量相差不大：外面一股力，中间一根绳。

examples.en: He pulled the chair closer to the fire.
examples.cn: 他把椅子拉近火边。

examples.en: The nurse pulled the sheet back to check the wound.
examples.cn: 护士把床单拉开查看伤口。

examples.en: She felt the pull of the old town and went back.
examples.cn: 她感受到老城的吸引力，于是回去了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「扑」——人往前一扑，抓住东西就往回拽，记住 pull 是拉。

root: 古英语 pullian（揪、拽），属日耳曼语层，无可靠拉丁同族词；由「手攥住往后拽」这一动作，发展出拔出、拉伤、拉力、吸引力与影响力诸义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hand closing on something and drawing it back; the senses divide into moving a whole object, extracting a part, straining a muscle, the force itself, and social leverage.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「手攥住东西往回拽」；义项由此分为移动整个物体、取出其中一部分、拉伤肌肉、力本身，以及社会上的影响力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands gripping a thick rope, feet braced on the ground, drawing it back inch by inch.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手攥住粗绳，双脚蹬地，一寸寸把绳子拽回来。

branches.en: a door dragged open against a stiff hinge
branches.cn: 顶着发涩的合页把门拽开

branches.en: a tooth eased out of its socket
branches.cn: 一颗牙从牙槽里被取出来

branches.en: a runner stopping short with a torn calf
branches.cn: 短跑者突然停下，小腿拉伤

branches.en: the moon lifting a whole sea
branches.cn: 月亮把整片海拉起来

branches.en: a name that opens doors without a key
branches.cn: 一个不用钥匙就能开门的名字

intro.en: The word is held together by an Old English verb of plucking, the English verb itself, two native suffixes, and three compounds built on the same gesture.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「揪、拽」的古英语动词、英语动词本身、两个本族后缀，以及三个建立在同一动作上的复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 脉搏；脉冲；搏动；脉动；活力
definition_en: the regular beating of blood in the arteries, a short sharp burst of electricity or sound, the act of throbbing, and the lively beat of a place or group
core_image: 指尖按在手腕内侧，皮肤下有一记一记的跳动传上来
scene: 手指压在手腕内侧，安静的房间里，那串规律的小跳动先慢后快。The doctor counted her pulse and wrote the number on the chart.
sceneCN: 这里 pulse 是「脉搏」（第 1 个义项：血液被心脏压入动脉时的规律搏动）；句意为医生数了她的脉搏，把数字写在病历上。图中可辨识物件：按在腕上的指尖、病历夹、笔。

pos.zh: 脉搏；脉冲；活力
搏动；脉动；跳动

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 puls- 加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「有规律地搏动」
由 pulsate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「搏动；脉动」
由表示「向内」的前缀 im- 加拉丁 pulsus 构成，义为「冲动；推动力」

senses.title: The regular beat of blood in the arteries
senses.definition: the regular beating of blood that can be felt at the wrist or neck as the heart pumps
senses.definitionCN: 心脏泵血时在手腕或颈部能摸到的规律搏动
senses.example: The nurse felt for a pulse at his wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在他手腕上摸脉搏。
senses.why: Latin pulsus meant a beat or a blow, so the word names the little hammering that the heart sends out along the arteries.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pulsus 意为「敲击、打击」，所以这个词指心脏顺着动脉送出的那一下下敲击。

senses.title: A short sharp burst of electricity or sound
senses.definition: a brief, sharp surge of electrical current, light or sound that rises and falls quickly
senses.definitionCN: 电流、光或声音短暂而尖锐的一次起落
senses.example: The device sends a pulse every second.
senses.exampleCN: 这个装置每秒发出一个脉冲。
senses.why: A pulse in physics is one beat of a signal, and the sense comes straight from the beating of the heart: a single rise and fall, then silence.
senses.whyCN: 物理学里的脉冲是信号的一记跳动，这个义项直接来自心跳：一次起落，然后是静默。

senses.title: The steady life or energy of a place or group
senses.definition: the lively, continuing energy that a place, group or activity seems to have
senses.definitionCN: 某个地方、群体或活动呈现出的持续生气与律动
senses.example: He could feel the pulse of the crowd quicken.
senses.exampleCN: 他能感到人群的脉动加快了。
senses.why: A busy street or a crowd beats with small movements the way a body does, so the medical word is borrowed for collective energy.
senses.whyCN: 热闹的街道或人群像身体一样以小动作跳动，于是这个医学词被借去指集体的活力。

senses.title: To beat or throb regularly
senses.definition: to beat or throb with a regular rhythm, as blood or music does
senses.definitionCN: 像血液或音乐那样按规律节奏跳动
senses.example: The music pulsed through the floor of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐透过大厅的地板一下下震动。
senses.why: The verb is the noun turned into action: whatever produces a pulse can be said to pulse, from an artery to a bass line.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词转成动作：凡能产生一次搏动的东西，都能说 pulse，从动脉到低音节奏皆是如此。

intro.en: Pulse comes through Old French from Latin pulsus, a beat or a blow, which is the past participle of pellere, to drive or strike.
intro.cn: pulse 经古法语来自拉丁语 pulsus（敲打、跳动），而 pulsus 是动词 pellere（推动、击打）的过去分词。

items.en: Pellere meant to drive, push or strike, and it supplied the family of beating words in Latin.
items.cn: pellere 意为推动、撞击，拉丁语中一整族表示「跳动、敲打」的词都由它派生。

items.en: Pulsus, the past participle, meant a beat or a blow, and was used for the beating of the heart and of the pulse.
items.cn: 过去分词 pulsus 意为敲击、跳动，用来指心脏和脉管的搏动。

items.en: Old French took the noun as pouls or puls, keeping the medical sense of the beat felt at the wrist.
items.cn: 古法语把名词写作 pouls 或 puls，保留了「腕上能摸到的搏动」这一医学义。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word as pulse and used it both for the heartbeat and for a measured beat in general.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 pulse，既指心跳，也泛指有节律的敲击。

items.en: Modern English extends pulse to electrical and sound signals, to any lively rhythm, and to the verb meaning to throb.
items.cn: 现代英语把 pulse 扩展到电信号与声信号、任何有生气的节奏，以及表示「搏动」的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that share the shape of pulse but not its history; the near-meaning group collects other words for a regular beat.
note.cn: 形近组收外形与 pulse 相近但并不同源的词；近义组收其他表示规律跳动的词。

entries.definition: A small bag for money, or to draw the lips tight.
entries.definitionCN: 装钱的小包，或把嘴唇收紧。

entries.definition: Added to; also the sign that marks addition.
entries.definitionCN: 加上；也指表示加号的符号。

entries.definition: To follow someone or something in order to catch it.
entries.definitionCN: 为了抓住而追赶。

entries.definition: A star that sends out regular radio pulses.
entries.definitionCN: 规律发出射电脉冲的星体。

entries.definition: To strike repeatedly, or a regular stroke of sound.
entries.definitionCN: 反复敲击，或规律的一记声响。

entries.definition: To beat strongly and painfully, as a wound does.
entries.definitionCN: 像伤口那样强烈而带痛地跳动。

entries.definition: One complete cycle of the heart's pumping.
entries.definitionCN: 心脏泵血的一次完整周期。

entries.definition: A regular pattern of beats or movements.
entries.definitionCN: 节拍或动作的规律型式。

normalIntro.en: The word is Latin for a blow, and the whole family keeps that single strike repeated at a steady interval.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词在拉丁语里意为「一击」，整个词族都保留着同一记敲击按固定间隔反复出现的意思。

normal.en: Pulse is Latin pulsus, a beat, from pellere, to strike, so the word begins as a blow rather than as blood.
normal.cn: pulse 是拉丁 pulsus（一击），出自 pellere（击打），所以这个词起点是敲击而不是血。

normal.en: Pulsate adds -ate to the same stem: to keep striking, therefore to throb.
normal.cn: pulsate 在同一词干后加 -ate：不断敲击，因此是搏动。

normal.en: Impulse puts in- in front of pulsus: a push coming into you from outside.
normal.cn: impulse 在 pulsus 前加 in-：一股从外面推到你身上的力。

normal.en: Take someone's pulse is the oldest use, because the wrist is where the beating is easiest to feel.
normal.cn: take someone's pulse 是最老的用法，因为手腕上最容易摸到搏动。

normal.en: An electric pulse is one beat of a signal, with silence on either side, exactly like a single heartbeat.
normal.cn: 电脉冲是信号的一记跳动，两侧都是静默，和一次心跳完全一样。

abstract.en: A pulse is a rhythm you can prove with your fingertips, which is why the word suits both blood and music.
abstract.cn: 脉搏是一种可以用指尖证明的节奏，所以这个词既适合血液也适合音乐。

abstract.en: Everything alive here is described by what it does at intervals, not by what it is at rest.
abstract.cn: 这里凡是活着的东西，都用它隔一段时间就做一次的事来描述，而不是静止时的样子。

abstract.en: A city can have a pulse only because people agree to move at the same hours.
abstract.cn: 城市之所以有脉动，只因为人们同意在同一批时段里活动。

examples.en: Her pulse was fast but steady.
examples.cn: 她的脉搏很快，但很平稳。

examples.en: The sensor records every pulse of light.
examples.cn: 传感器记录每一束光脉冲。

examples.en: Drums pulsed somewhere behind the crowd.
examples.cn: 人群后方某处有鼓声一下下震动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「拍死」——手指按在腕上，那一下下拍到皮肤上的跳动，就是 pulse 脉搏。

root: 拉丁语 pellere（推动、击打）→ 过去分词 pulsus（一击、跳动）→ 古法语 pouls → 英语 pulse；核心是「按固定节奏的一记敲击」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one beat repeated at intervals; the senses divide into the heartbeat felt at the wrist, the single beat of a signal, the liveliness of a group, and the verb for throbbing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「按间隔反复出现的一记跳动」；义项由此分为腕上摸到的心跳、信号的一记脉冲、群体的活力，以及表示搏动的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two fingertips pressed to the inside of a wrist, a small regular knock rising through the skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根手指按在手腕内侧，皮肤下传上来一记记规律的轻敲。

branches.en: two fingers finding the beat under the skin
branches.cn: 两根手指在皮肤下找到那记跳动

branches.en: a single flash from a small device
branches.cn: 小装置发出的一次闪动

branches.en: a crowd whose noise rises and falls together
branches.cn: 喧声一起一落的人群

branches.en: drums shaking a wooden floor
branches.cn: 鼓声震动木地板

branches.en: the same rhythm inside a body and inside a street
branches.cn: 身体里与街道上同一种节律

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin verb for striking, its participle, the noun that came to English, and the English endings that build the verb and the noun of beating.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示击打的拉丁动词、它的过去分词、传入英语的名词，以及构成「搏动」动词与名词的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 泵；抽水机；用泵抽送；打气；投入（资金）；上下抽动
definition_en: a machine that forces liquid or gas through a pipe; to move liquid or gas with such a machine; to fill something with air; to pour money into something; to move a handle or a limb up and down
core_image: 院子里一台旧铁泵，手柄一压一抬，清澈的水就顺着铁嘴流进木桶
scene: 院子里那台旧铁家伙生了锈，可手柄压下去再抬起来，水还是照样从铁嘴里涌出来。The old pump in the yard still lifts water from the well.
sceneCN: 这里 pump 是「泵、抽水机」（第 1 个义项：靠往复运动把水或气强制送出的机器）；句意为院子里那台旧泵仍能把井水抽上来。图中可辨识物件：铸铁泵体、手柄、木桶。

pos.zh: 泵；抽水机；油泵
用泵抽送；打气；投入；上下抽动

derivatives.zh: pump 加表人或表工具的后缀 -er，指操作泵的人，也指消防泵车
pump 与 house 复合，指安放泵的泵房
pump 加 -ing 构成的动名词，指抽送这一动作

senses.title: A machine that forces liquid or gas along
senses.definition: a machine that pushes liquid or gas through a pipe or into a container by pressure or suction
senses.definitionCN: 靠压力或吸力把液体、气体压过管道或压进容器的机器
senses.example: The village well has an iron pump beside it.
senses.exampleCN: 村口那口井旁边有一台铁泵。
senses.why: The word first named a simple wooden device worked by hand in mines and ships, and the machine kept the name even after steam and electricity replaced the handle.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指矿井与船上那种靠手压的木制装置，后来即便蒸汽与电力取代了手柄，机器仍旧叫这个名字。

senses.title: To move liquid or gas with such a machine
senses.definition: to make liquid or gas flow by means of a pump or by a similar pushing and sucking motion
senses.definitionCN: 借助泵或类似的推吸动作使液体、气体流动
senses.example: They pumped the flooded cellar dry overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一夜之间把灌水的地窖抽干了。
senses.why: Once the tool has a name, the work it performs takes the same word as a verb, so pumping is simply the machine's action applied to a place.
senses.whyCN: 工具一旦有了名字，它干的活就用同一个词作动词，所以 pumping 不过是把机器的动作施加到某个地方。

senses.title: To fill something with air
senses.definition: to force air into a tyre, a ball or a mattress until it is firm
senses.definitionCN: 把空气压进轮胎、球或床垫，直到它们鼓起来
senses.example: He pumped up the back tyre before the ride.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前他给后胎打了气。
senses.why: Air is a gas, so the same verb that moves water through a pipe also pushes air into a closed rubber space until it tightens.
senses.whyCN: 空气也是一种气体，于是原本把水送过管道的动词，也被用来把空气压进封闭的橡胶空间，直到它绷紧。

senses.title: To pour money or resources into something
senses.definition: to put large amounts of money, energy or information into something in a steady stream
senses.definitionCN: 把钱、精力或信息以持续不断的方式大量投入某事
senses.example: The city has pumped millions into the new line.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市已为新线路投入了数百万资金。
senses.why: Money is made to flow like water through a pipe, so the image of forcing a fluid steadily in one direction is applied to funding.
senses.whyCN: 钱被安排得像水一样从管子里流，于是「把流体稳定压向一方」的形象被搬用到资金上。

senses.title: To move up and down or in and out repeatedly
senses.definition: to move a handle, a limb or a part of the body quickly up and down or in and out
senses.definitionCN: 把手柄、肢体或身体某部分快速地上下来回或进出移动
senses.example: His heart pumped hard after the long climb.
senses.exampleCN: 长途爬坡之后，他的心脏剧烈跳动。
senses.why: The handle of an old pump must be worked up and down, and that repeated motion became a sense of its own, applied to fists, pedals and a beating heart.
senses.whyCN: 旧泵的手柄必须一上一下地压，这个反复的动作本身也成了一个义项，被用到拳头、踏板和跳动的心脏上。

intro.en: Pump appears in late Middle English, probably borrowed from Middle Dutch or Middle Low German pompe; the further origin is uncertain and no reliable Latin source is recorded, so the Latin comparison is left empty.
intro.cn: pump 出现于中古英语后期，一般认为借自中古荷兰语或中古低地德语的 pompe；更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁语源头，因此拉丁对照留空。

items.en: The word is first recorded in English in the fifteenth century as pumpe, naming a device for lifting water out of a ship or a mine.
items.cn: 这个词十五世纪以 pumpe 的形式首次见于英语，指把水从船上或矿井里提上来的装置。

items.en: It is generally thought to be borrowed from Middle Dutch or Middle Low German pompe, the word used by the sailors and miners who worked such devices.
items.cn: 一般认为它借自中古荷兰语或中古低地德语的 pompe，那是操作这类装置的水手与矿工所用的词。

items.en: Beyond that point the trail is uncertain; some scholars link the form to a sucking or thumping sound, but no source is agreed.
items.cn: 再往前追溯就不确定了；有学者把这个形式与吸吮或撞击的声音联系起来，但没有公认的源头。

items.en: By the seventeenth century pump covers ship pumps, mine pumps and the verb, and the handle-driven machine spreads to wells and gardens.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，pump 已涵盖船泵、矿泵及相应动词，这种手柄驱动的机器也推广到水井与园圃。

items.en: Modern English pumps petrol, air and money, and the up-and-down motion survives in phrases such as pump iron and pump a fist.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pump 输送汽油、空气和金钱，而上下抽动的动作仍留在 pump iron、pump a fist 这类说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that differ from pump by a single consonant; the near-meaning group collects other verbs for moving liquid, air or money in a steady flow.
note.cn: 形近组收与 pump 只差一个辅音的词；近义组收其他表示「让液体、空气或钱持续流动」的动词。

entries.definitionCN: 轻轻的一撞，或表面上隆起的一块。

entries.definition: To make liquid flow away from a place.

entries.definition: To fill something with air or gas.

entries.definition: The force that draws liquid or air into a space.
entries.definitionCN: 把液体或空气吸入某处的力。

normalIntro.en: The word names a hand-worked device for lifting water, and every later sense keeps the idea of forcing something to move in one direction.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词原本指靠手操作的提水装置，后来每个义项都保留着「把东西强制推向一个方向」的意思。

normal.en: Pump entered English in the fifteenth century, probably from Dutch or Low German pompe, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
normal.cn: pump 十五世纪进入英语，一般认为来自荷兰语或低地德语的 pompe，更早的源头不确定。

normal.en: Pumper adds -er: the person who works the pump, or the fire engine that carries one.
normal.cn: pumper 加 -er：操作泵的人，或载着泵的消防车。

normal.en: Pump up works the same way as a bicycle pump: air goes in and the rubber tightens.
normal.cn: pump up 的作用就像打气筒：空气进去，橡胶绷紧。

normal.en: Pump money into a project borrows the pipe: the flow is steady and aimed at one place.
normal.cn: pump money into 借用了管子的形象：流量稳定，而且只朝一个地方。

normal.en: Pump iron is not about water at all; it keeps only the up-and-down motion of the handle.
normal.cn: pump iron 与水和气都无关，它只保留了手柄一上一下的动作。

abstract.en: A pump is a promise that what is below can be brought up, if someone keeps working the handle.
abstract.cn: 泵是一种承诺：只要有人持续压动手柄，下面的东西就能被提上来。

abstract.en: The same verb serves water, air and money because all three can be made to flow in one direction.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词同时服务水、空气和钱，因为这三样都能被逼着朝一个方向流动。

abstract.en: Repetition is the whole machine: one stroke does little, ten thousand strokes empty a flooded room.
abstract.cn: 重复就是整台机器：一次行程微不足道，上万次就能抽干一间灌水的屋子。

examples.en: The farmers pump water from the river into the fields.
examples.cn: 农民把河水抽到田里。

examples.en: She pumped up her bike tyres before leaving.
examples.cn: 出发前她给自行车轮胎打了气。

examples.en: Investors pumped more money into the project last spring.
examples.cn: 去年春天投资者向这个项目投入了更多资金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「啪噗」——手柄一压，管口啪噗一声，水就上来了，记住 pump 是泵。

root: 中古英语后期 pumpe，一般认为借自中古荷兰语或中古低地德语 pompe（提水装置），更早来源不确定，无可靠拉丁同族词；核心是「靠反复推压把流体送出去」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hand-worked device that pushes fluid one way; the senses divide into the machine, the act of moving liquid, filling with air, pouring money in, and the up-and-down stroke itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「靠人力把流体朝一个方向推出去的装置」；义项由此分为机器本身、抽送液体、充气、投入资金，以及那个上下压动的动作。

core.cn: 核心意象：院子里一台铁泵，手柄压下又抬起，清水流进木桶。

branches.cn: 在气嘴下渐渐绷紧的轮胎

branches.cn: 一次次挥向空中的拳头

intro.en: The word is held together by a Middle English noun of uncertain borrowing, its Dutch or Low German ancestor, and the English endings and compounds that grew from it.
intro.cn: 这个词由来源不确定的中古英语名词、它在荷兰语或低地德语中的祖先，以及由它长出的英语后缀与复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 用拳猛击；打孔；冲床；打孔器；冲击力；潘趣酒
definition_en: to hit someone hard with a closed fist; to make a hole in something with a tool; a tool or machine that cuts holes; the force of a blow or of words; a mixed drink of juice and spirits
core_image: 一只握紧的拳头从肩后送出，正中沙袋，袋面凹下去又弹回来
scene: 拳台上铃声刚停，两个人贴着围绳绕圈，脚步轻轻点地。He threw a punch that landed on the other man's shoulder.
sceneCN: 这里 punch 是「用拳猛击」（第 1 个义项：握拳用力打向对方）；句意为他挥出一拳，落在对方肩上。图中可辨识物件：拳套、沙袋、围绳。

pos.zh: 用拳猛击；打孔；按键
一拳；冲击力；打孔器；冲床；潘趣酒

derivatives.zh: punch 加表人后缀 -er，指挥拳的人，也指打孔的人或打孔器
punch 加形容词后缀 -y，义为「简短有力的；冲击力强的」
punch 与 up 复合，英式英语指互殴、打斗

senses.title: To hit hard with a closed fist
senses.definition: to hit a person or thing hard with a fist
senses.definitionCN: 用握紧的拳头重重打人或打物
senses.example: He punched the bag until his arms ached.
senses.exampleCN: 他一直打沙袋，直到两臂酸痛。
senses.why: The verb probably comes from the older sense of pricking or thrusting, and a blow with the fist is a thrust made with the whole arm.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词大概来自更早的「刺、戳」义，而用拳打人正是用整条手臂做出的一次戳击。

senses.title: To make a hole with a tool
senses.definition: to make a hole in paper, metal or leather with a sharp tool or machine
senses.definitionCN: 用尖锐工具或机器在纸、金属、皮革上打出孔洞
senses.example: The clerk punched a hole in my ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 职员在我的票上打了个孔。
senses.why: A punch is first a pointed tool driven through material, so the verb keeps the image of a small sharp point entering and leaving.
senses.whyCN: punch 最初指被压穿材料的尖头工具，因此动词保留了「一个尖点进入又穿出」的形象。

senses.title: A tool or machine that cuts holes
senses.definition: a tool or machine with a sharp end that cuts holes or stamps shapes into material
senses.definitionCN: 带尖头、能在材料上打孔或压出形状的工具或机器
senses.example: The workshop bought a new punch for the steel plates.
senses.exampleCN: 车间为钢板买了一台新冲床。
senses.why: The name of the tool outlives the act: what was once a hand-held point becomes a heavy machine, and both are still called a punch.
senses.whyCN: 工具的名字比动作更长寿：曾经的手持尖锥变成了沉重的机器，两者至今都叫 punch。

senses.title: Force or impact, in a blow or in words
senses.definition: the power to strike hard, whether of a blow, a drink or a remark
senses.definitionCN: 击打、饮品或言语带来的强烈力度与感染力
senses.example: Her closing sentence had real punch.
senses.exampleCN: 她结尾那句话很有冲击力。
senses.why: Something that hits hard leaves a mark, so the noun for the blow is used for whatever produces a similar jolt, including a line of argument.
senses.whyCN: 打得重的东西会留下痕迹，于是「一击」这个名词被用来指产生同样震动的东西，包括一句论证。

senses.title: A mixed drink of fruit juice and spirits
senses.definition: a drink made by mixing fruit juice, sugar and spirits, usually served in a large bowl
senses.definitionCN: 把果汁、糖与烈酒调在一起、通常盛在大碗里供应的饮品
senses.example: A bowl of punch stood at the end of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌子尽头摆着一碗潘趣酒。
senses.why: This sense is not related to the fist or the tool at all: it comes from Hindi panch, five, for a drink once mixed from five ingredients.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项与拳头、工具完全无关：它来自印地语 panch（五），因为这种饮品从前用五种配料调成。

intro.en: Punch has two separate histories that happen to share one spelling: the fist-and-hole word goes back through French to Latin pungere, to prick, while the drink comes from Hindi panch, five.
intro.cn: punch 有两条彼此无关的历史，只是恰好共用一个拼法：表示拳击与打孔的词经法语上溯到拉丁语 pungere（刺），而表示饮品的那条则来自印地语 panch（五）。

items.en: Pungere meant to prick or pierce, and it is the source of the Latin nouns for a point and for a pricking pain.
items.cn: pungere 意为刺、戳穿，是拉丁语中表示「尖点」与「刺痛」的名词的来源。

items.en: Punctum meant a prick or a point, literally something made by piercing, and it underlies puncture and punctual.
items.cn: punctum 意为刺痕或一点，字面就是「被戳出来的东西」，是 puncture 与 punctual 的来源。

items.en: Old French poinçon named an awl or a pointed tool, and the verb ponchonner meant to prick or stamp with it.
items.cn: 古法语 poinçon 指锥子一类尖头工具，动词 ponchonner 意为用它刺或冲压。

items.en: Middle English borrowed punch as a verb for pricking or perforating, and by the sixteenth century it also meant striking with the fist.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 punch 作动词，指刺穿、打孔；到十六世纪也指用拳头打。

items.en: The drink is a separate borrowing of the seventeenth century from Hindi panch, five, for a bowl mixed from five ingredients; it shares no root with the fist.
items.cn: 表示饮品的那条是十七世纪从印地语 panch（五）单独借入的，指用五种配料调成的一碗酒；它与拳头义毫无词根关系。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that rhyme with punch but are unrelated; the near-meaning group collects verbs for hitting and nouns for a blow.
note.cn: 形近组收与 punch 押韵但彼此无关的词；近义组收表示打击的动词与表示一击的名词。

entries.definition: A group of things gathered or tied together.
entries.definitionCN: 聚拢或扎在一起的一束东西。

entries.definition: The meal eaten in the middle of the day.
entries.definitionCN: 中午吃的那顿饭。

entries.definition: To squeeze a small fold of skin between finger and thumb.
entries.definitionCN: 用拇指与食指捏住一小块皮肤。

entries.definition: A large rounded stomach.
entries.definitionCN: 凸起的大肚子。

entries.definition: To strike someone or something with force.
entries.definitionCN: 用力打人或打物。

entries.definition: To hit something deliberately, often with the hand or a weapon.
entries.definitionCN: 有意地用手或器械击打。

entries.definition: A quick short punch, especially in boxing.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指拳击中的快速短拳。

entries.definition: To hit something heavily, making a dull sound.
entries.definitionCN: 重重击打并发出闷响。

normalIntro.en: Two unrelated words wear the same spelling: one is a Latin point driven through material or into a face, the other is a five-part drink from India.
normalIntro.cn: 两个互不相干的词穿着同一个拼法：一个是把拉丁语的尖点压进材料或打进脸上的动作，另一个是来自印度、由五样东西调成的酒。

normal.en: Punch the verb goes back through French to Latin pungere, to prick, which is why a pointed tool and a fist blow share the word.
normal.cn: 动词 punch 经法语上溯到拉丁 pungere（刺），所以尖头工具与拳击共用一个词。

normal.en: Punctum, a point or prick, gives English puncture and punctual, both still about a small sharp point or an exact point in time.
normal.cn: punctum（点、刺痕）给英语带来 puncture 与 punctual，两者仍与尖点或准确的时间点有关。

normal.en: The punch that cuts paper is the oldest tool sense; the machine in a workshop grew from that hand-held point.
normal.cn: 在纸上打孔的 punch 是最早的工具义，车间里的机器正是从那个手持尖锥长出来的。

normal.en: Punch the drink is a different word from Hindi panch, five, named for five ingredients in one bowl.
normal.cn: 表示饮品的 punch 是另一个词，来自印地语 panch（五），因一碗里放五样配料而得名。

normal.en: Pack a punch and punch line both use the blow as a metaphor: something lands hard on the listener.
normal.cn: pack a punch 与 punch line 都把这一击当比喻：有什么东西重重落在听者身上。

abstract.en: One spelling, two histories: a point that pierces, and five things stirred in a bowl.
abstract.cn: 一个拼法，两段历史：一个刺穿的尖点，和五样在碗里搅匀的东西。

abstract.en: A punch is short and concentrated, which is why the word also means the force that a sentence can carry.
abstract.cn: 一拳短促而集中，所以这个词也用来指一句话能带出的力量。

abstract.en: Words that land hardest usually contain the fewest of them.
abstract.cn: 最能打中人的话，往往用的词最少。

examples.en: He punched the door in frustration.
examples.cn: 他懊恼地一拳打在门上。

examples.en: The guard punched my ticket twice.
examples.cn: 检票员在我的票上打了两个孔。

examples.en: They served lemonade and fruit punch in the garden.
examples.cn: 他们在花园里供应柠檬水和水果潘趣酒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「乓啷」——拳头一出，乓啷一声落在沙袋上；记住 punch 是出拳，也别忘了那碗五种料调成的潘趣酒。

root: 两条互不相干的来源：一为拉丁语 pungere（刺）→ punctum（刺痕、点）→ 古法语 poinçon（尖锥）→ 英语 punch（打孔、出拳）；一为印地语 panch（五）→ 英语 punch（潘趣酒）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a sharp point driven in hard; the senses divide into the fist blow, the hole it makes, the tool that makes it, the force felt from it, and the unrelated five-part drink.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「一个尖点被重重压进去」；义项由此分为挥拳、打出的孔、打孔的工具、感受到的冲击力，以及与它们无关的五料饮品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed fist driven forward from the shoulder, landing on a sandbag that dents and swings back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只握紧的拳头从肩后送出，打在沙袋上，袋面凹下又荡回来。

branches.en: a fist landing on canvas
branches.cn: 落在帆布上的拳头

branches.en: a neat round hole in a ticket
branches.cn: 票面上一个整齐的圆孔

branches.en: a heavy press biting into steel plate

intro.cn: 主线由表示刺的拉丁动词、指「点」的拉丁名词、法语工具名，以及由它们构成的英语后缀共同支撑；表示饮品的那条完全在这个词族之外。

definition_zh: 准时的；守时的；按时的；（术语）点的，点状的
definition_en: arriving or happening at the agreed time, and, in technical use, relating to a single point
core_image: 站台上的钟走到约定那一分，一个人正好踏进车门
scene: 清晨的站台上，列车还没停稳，一个提着公文包的人已经站在黄线后看表。She is always punctual, reaching the office before anyone else.
sceneCN: 这里取「准时的」（第 1 个义项：人按约定时间到达）；句意是她总是很准时，比谁都先到办公室。黄线后看表的人影就是线索。

pos.zh: 准时的；守时的；按时的；（术语）点的

derivatives.zh: 由 punctual 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「准时地；按时地」
由 punctual 加名词后缀 -ity（源自拉丁 -itas）构成，义为「守时；准时」
由否定前缀 un- 加 punctual 构成，义为「不准时的；常迟到的」

senses.title: Arriving at the agreed time
senses.definition: of a person, arriving at the time that was agreed or arranged
senses.definitionCN: 指人按约定或安排好的时间到达
senses.example: The teacher is punctual and never keeps a class waiting.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老师很守时，从不让全班等她。
senses.why: The word began as punctualis, 'relating to a point', and a fixed hour is exactly a point on the clock that a person chooses to land on.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初写作 punctualis，意思是「与点有关的」；约定的那个钟点正是时间上的一个「点」，守时的人就是让自己的到达落在这个点上。

senses.title: Happening at the fixed hour
senses.definition: of an event or arrangement, starting or taking place at the exact time set
senses.definitionCN: 指事件或安排在其设定的准确时刻开始或发生
senses.example: The punctual start of the ceremony surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 典礼准点开始，让所有人都感到意外。
senses.why: If one person can land on the point of an hour, so can a ceremony; the same picture moves from a single arrival to the timing of a whole event.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个人可以落在钟点这个「点」上，一场典礼也可以；同一个画面从单个人的到达，扩大为整场活动的时间安排。

senses.title: Done without delay
senses.definition: of an action such as payment or reply, done at the time it was promised
senses.definitionCN: 指付款、回复等行为在承诺的时间完成
senses.example: Punctual payment of the rent keeps the contract in good standing.
senses.exampleCN: 按时交房租能让合同保持有效。
senses.why: The point on the clock is also a deadline; when the action lands on it, the habit of being on time becomes a quality of the act itself.
senses.whyCN: 钟点上的那个点同时也是一条期限；当行为正好落在这个点上，「守时」就从人的习惯变成了行为本身的属性。

senses.title: (Technical) belonging to a point
senses.definition: in technical writing, existing at or relating to a single point rather than to an area
senses.definitionCN: 在技术性文字中，指存在于某一点上或与单点有关的，而不是涉及一个面
senses.example: The model treats each charge as punctual, with no size at all.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型把每个电荷都当作点来处理，完全不考虑其大小。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer, kept almost unchanged: punctum is a point made by a prick, so the adjective still says 'of a point' before it ever says 'on time'.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层，几乎没有改变：punctum 是被刺出来的一个点，所以这个形容词最早说的就是「关于点的」，后来才说「准时的」。

intro.en: Punctual goes back to the Latin verb for pricking, whose noun punctum means a point; the modern sense of keeping time grew out of landing exactly on a point of the clock.
intro.cn: punctual 可追到拉丁语中表示「刺」的动词，其名词 punctum 意为「点」；现代「守时」义正是从「落在钟面的某一点上」长出来的。

items.en: Pungere meant to prick or to pierce, and it is the physical act behind the whole family.
items.cn: pungere 意为刺、扎，是整族词背后那个具体的动作。

items.en: A punctum was the small mark left by a prick, and from that it came to mean a point in space or in writing.
items.cn: punctum 是刺一下留下的小痕，由此指空间或文字中的一个点。

items.en: Medieval Latin punctualis meant relating to a point and was used for things fixed to one exact point.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 punctualis 意为「与点有关的」，用于指固定在某一确切点上的事物。

items.en: English took the adjective in the seventeenth century, first in the technical sense and then for keeping to an appointed hour.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词，先用其技术义，随后用来指遵守约定的钟点。

items.en: Modern English uses punctual almost only for people and events that keep time, while the older sense survives in technical writing.
items.cn: 现代英语几乎只用 punctual 指守时的人和准点的事，较古的「点的」义则保留在技术文字里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb of pricking and its noun for a point; the near-meaning group gathers words for keeping to time.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「刺」动词及其「点」名词上的词；近义组收表示遵守时间的词。

entries.definition: The marks that divide writing, named from the same Latin word for a point.
entries.definitionCN: 标点符号，名字来自同一个表示「点」的拉丁词。

entries.definition: A small hole made by something sharp.
entries.definitionCN: 被尖锐物扎出的小孔。

entries.definition: Sharp in taste or smell, as if pricking the nose.
entries.definitionCN: 味道或气味刺激的，像扎鼻子一样。

entries.definition: Extremely careful about the small details of behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 对行为细节极为讲究的。

entries.definition: Done at once, without delay.
entries.definitionCN: 立刻完成的，不拖延的。

entries.definition: Happening at a good or useful moment.
entries.definitionCN: 发生在合适或有用时机的。

entries.definition: Happening at the same times and in the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 按时、按固定方式发生的。

normalIntro.en: The word starts from a dot pricked into a surface, and its family keeps returning to points and to the hours that people agree on.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从刺在表面上的一个小点开始，同族词反复回到「点」以及人们约定的小时。

normal.en: Pungere means to prick and punctum is the dot left by the prick, so the word starts from a single point.
normal.cn: pungere 意为刺，punctum 是刺出来的那个小点，所以这个词的起点是一个「点」。

normal.en: The hour you agree on is a point on the clock, and a punctual person lands exactly on it.
normal.cn: 约定的小时是钟面上的一个点，守时的人正好让到达落在这个点上。

normal.en: Punctuality is built with -ity, and it names the habit rather than one arrival.
normal.cn: punctuality 加 -ity 构成名词，指这种习惯，而不是某一次到达。

normal.en: Punctually adds -ly and describes the way an action is carried out.
normal.cn: punctually 加 -ly，用来说明动作是怎样完成的。

normal.en: Punctuation and puncture share the same point: one marks a page, the other marks a surface.
normal.cn: punctuation 与 puncture 共享同一个「点」：一个点在纸面上，一个扎在物体表面。

abstract.en: Being on time is a small promise kept, which is how a word for a dot became a word about trust.
abstract.cn: 守时是一个被兑现的小承诺，那个表示「点」的词就这样变成了关于信任的词。

abstract.en: A clock turns time into points, and every appointment is a point two people agree to meet at.
abstract.cn: 钟把时间变成一个个点，每一次约会就是两个人约定相见的一个点。

abstract.en: The distance between almost and exactly is the whole subject of this word.
abstract.cn: 「差一点」与「正好」之间的距离，正是这个词的全部主题。

examples.en: The teacher is punctual and never keeps a class waiting.
examples.cn: 这位老师很守时，从不让全班等她。

examples.en: Punctual payment of the rent keeps the contract in good standing.
examples.cn: 按时交房租能让合同保持有效。

examples.en: The punctual start of the ceremony surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 典礼准点开始，让所有人都感到意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音近「碰克秋」——听着像「碰巧赶上」，正好在那一点赶到，就是准时。

root: 拉丁语 pungere（刺）→ punctum（刺出的小点）→ 中世纪拉丁语 punctualis（与点有关的），十七世纪进入英语，由「落在某一点上」发展出「守时」义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is landing on a single point of time; the senses divide into a person who arrives, an event that begins, an action done on time, and the old technical sense of a point.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「落在时间的某一个点上」；义项分成到达的人、开始的事、按时完成的行为，以及古老的「点」这一术语义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a station clock reaching the agreed minute as a traveller steps through the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：站台上的钟走到约定的那一分，一个旅人正好踏进车门。

branches.en: a commuter standing behind the yellow line, checking the time
branches.cn: 通勤者站在黄线后看表

branches.en: a ceremony beginning as the clock ticks the hour
branches.cn: 钟声敲响时开始的典礼

branches.en: rent paid on the first day of the month
branches.cn: 每月第一天付掉的房租

branches.en: a diagram where every charge is reduced to a dot
branches.cn: 把每个电荷都简化成一个点的示意图

branches.en: a person and a payment both landing on the agreed minute
branches.cn: 人与一笔钱都落在约定的那一刻

intro.en: A Latin verb of pricking and its noun for a point hold the word together, and Latin and English endings build the adjective, the adverb and the two nouns.
intro.cn: 表示「刺」的拉丁语动词及其「点」名词共同支撑这个词，拉丁语与英语的词尾再构成形容词、副词和两个名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pungere, to prick, punctum, a point, and the Medieval Latin adjective punctualis are the direct sources of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pungere（刺）、punctum（点）与中世纪拉丁语形容词 punctualis 是英语这个词的直接来源。

the habit of being on time

definition_zh: 惩罚；处罚；严厉对待；粗暴使用使损坏；重创（对手）；猛烈抨击；使身体极度疲惫
definition_en: to make someone suffer for a wrong, or to treat a person or thing so harshly that it is worn down
core_image: 木槌落下，犯错的人被带离座位，去承受自己招来的那阵疼痛
scene: 夜间巡查时，看守发现一名囚犯试图翻墙逃走，于是把他单独关进一间没有窗的小屋。The warden punished the prisoner by locking him alone in a windowless cell.
sceneCN: 这里指「因过错而使某人受苦」，对应第 1 个义项：让犯错者为自己的行为承担痛苦；句意为看守把企图逃跑的囚犯单独关进没有窗的小屋作为惩罚。画面要点：夜间走廊、翻墙的脚印、被关上的铁门；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 惩罚；处罚（及物动词，常与 for 连用说明过错）
严厉对待；粗暴使用使损坏（口语中可指物）

forms.label: 现在分词作形容词（折磨人的）

derivatives.zh: 由 punish 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作结果）→ 由「使人受苦这一动作」转为「所施加的那份痛苦或处罚」
由 punish 加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表能够被）→ 由「施加惩罚」转为「依法可以受罚的」
由 punish 加现在分词后缀 → 由「惩罚他人」转为形容「像惩罚一样消耗人的、折磨人的」
由 punish 加施事后缀（表施动者）→ 由「惩罚」这一动作转为「施加惩罚的那个人」
与 punish 同出拉丁 punire，加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向）→ 由「施加惩罚」转为「以惩罚为目的的、惩罚性的」
与 punish 同出拉丁 poena，经古法语形成名词 → 由「惩罚这一动作」转为「作为惩罚所付的那笔代价」

senses.title: To make someone suffer for a wrong
senses.definition: to cause a person who has done wrong to undergo pain, loss or hardship
senses.definitionCN: 使做错事的人经历痛苦、损失或艰难
senses.example: The company punished the clerk for leaking the file.
senses.exampleCN: 公司因那名职员泄露文件而惩罚了他。
senses.why: Latin punire meant to make someone pay for a wrong, so the core idea is not pain for its own sake but a debt being settled through suffering.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 punire 意为让某人为过错付出代价，所以核心并不是疼痛本身，而是一笔债通过受苦被结清。

senses.title: To sentence in a court
senses.definition: to impose a legal sentence on a convicted person
senses.definitionCN: 对已被定罪的人施加法律判决
senses.example: The court punished the fraud with five years in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭判处那名诈骗犯五年监禁。
senses.why: When the debt is collected by a court, the suffering is fixed by law, given a name and given a term.
senses.whyCN: 当这笔债由法庭来收取，痛苦就由法律确定，被赋予名称，也被赋予期限。

senses.title: To discipline a child or pupil
senses.definition: to correct a child or pupil by withdrawing something valued or by mild suffering
senses.definitionCN: 以收回孩子看重的某物或轻微的苦头来纠正其行为
senses.example: His parents punished him by cancelling the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 他父母取消旅行作为对他的惩罚。
senses.why: A household collects the same debt in miniature: a small wrong, a small withdrawal of what the child values.
senses.whyCN: 家庭以缩小的尺度收取同一笔债：小小的过错，配上小小地拿走孩子看重的东西。

senses.title: To treat someone with deliberate harshness
senses.titleCN: 刻意以严酷手段对待某人
senses.definition: to subject a person to prolonged harsh treatment, whether or not a rule was broken
senses.definitionCN: 使某人长时间承受严酷对待，不论是否真的违规
senses.example: The guards punished the prisoners by keeping them standing all night.
senses.exampleCN: 看守让囚犯整夜站立，以此折磨他们。
senses.why: Once pain is separated from the debt, any deliberate infliction of suffering can take the name, even where no rule exists to be broken.
senses.whyCN: 一旦疼痛与那笔债脱钩，任何刻意施加的痛苦都能叫这个名字，哪怕并不存在可供违反的规则。

senses.title: To damage something by rough use
senses.titleCN: 因粗暴使用而损坏某物
senses.definition: to wear out or damage an object by using it far harder than it was designed for
senses.definitionCN: 以远超设计承受的方式使用，使物品磨损或损坏
senses.example: Rough roads punish the tyres far more than smooth ones.
senses.exampleCN: 崎岖路面比平坦路面更伤轮胎。
senses.why: Objects cannot owe a debt, so the word transfers to rough treatment that makes a thing suffer wear, as if the thing were being made to pay.
senses.whyCN: 物品不可能欠债，于是这个词转到「粗暴对待使某物受损」上，仿佛那件东西也在被逼着付出代价。

senses.title: To defeat an opponent by a wide margin
senses.titleCN: 以压倒性优势重创对手
senses.definition: to beat an opponent so heavily that the defeat feels like a penalty
senses.definitionCN: 以极大差距击败对手，使这场失败如同一种惩罚
senses.example: The champions punished the visitors with four goals in twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军队在二十分钟内连进四球，重创了客队。
senses.why: A contest can turn a score into a debt, and a heavy defeat is that debt being collected all at once.
senses.whyCN: 比赛可以把比分变成一笔债，而一场惨败就是这笔债被一次性收走。

senses.title: To criticise sharply
senses.definition: to attack a person, work or idea with very severe public criticism
senses.definitionCN: 以极严厉的公开批评攻击某人、某作品或某观点
senses.example: The critics punished the film for its empty spectacle.
senses.exampleCN: 影评人猛烈抨击这部影片空洞的视觉堆砌。
senses.why: Words can inflict suffering too, so sharp criticism borrows the same verb and makes its target pay in reputation.
senses.whyCN: 言语也能造成痛苦，于是尖锐的批评借用了同一个动词，让对象以名声偿付。

senses.title: To exhaust the body through effort
senses.titleCN: 使身体因用力而极度疲惫
senses.definition: to strain the body so hard that the effort feels like a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 使身体承担极大负荷，让这种用力如同惩罚
senses.example: The steep climb punished legs that had not trained.
senses.exampleCN: 陡峭的山路让未经训练的腿吃尽苦头。
senses.why: The body itself can be made to pay for the effort demanded of it, so intense exertion completes the drift from moral debt to sheer physical cost.
senses.whyCN: 身体本身也能为被要求的努力付出代价，于是高强度消耗完成了从道德亏欠到纯粹身体代价的漂移。

intro.en: Punish came into English through Old French punir from Latin punire, an earlier form poenire built on poena 'penalty'. The same poena family also produced penal, penalty and punitive. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: punish 经古法语 punir 进入英语，上溯拉丁 punire，其较早形式 poenire 由 poena「罚」构成；同一个 poena 词族还生出 penal、penalty 与 punitive。年代均为约数。

items.en: The Greek noun poine named the price paid to settle a wrong, and it was borrowed into Latin as the starting point of this family.
items.cn: 希腊名词 poine 指为平息过错而付出的价，它被借入拉丁语，成为这一词族的起点。

items.en: Poena meant punishment and also the compensation that settled a wrong, and from it the verb poenire was formed.
items.cn: poena 既指处罚，也指平息过错的补偿，动词 poenire 由它构成。

items.en: Punire replaced the older poenire and meant to inflict a penalty, to avenge, to take vengeance for a wrong.
items.cn: punire 取代了较早的 poenire，意为施加处罚、报复、为过错索取代价。

items.en: Old French punir carried the Latin verb into the sense of correcting by pain, and English borrowed it around 1300.
items.cn: 古法语 punir 把这一拉丁动词带入「以痛苦纠正」的意思，英语大约在十四世纪初借入。

items.en: English punish first meant to inflict a legal penalty, then any painful correction, and finally rough handling of people or things.
items.cn: 英语 punish 最初指施加法律上的处罚，随后泛指任何带来痛苦的纠正，最后扩展到对人、对物的粗暴对待。

items.en: Punishment names the suffering as a result, punishable names what may be punished, and punitive names the intention behind a measure.
items.cn: punishment 把痛苦作为结果来命名，punishable 指可以受罚的，punitive 则指一项措施背后的惩罚意图。

note.en: The first group holds the same Latin family plus one mere look-alike; the second group offers near alternatives for the act of making someone suffer.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族的词，外加一个只是长得像的词；第二组是「使人受苦」这一动作的近义替代。

entries.definition: The noun naming the suffering imposed; the verb names the act of imposing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被施加的痛苦的名词；动词则指施加这一动作。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'liable to be punished'; it describes a legal status, not an act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「可受处罚的」形容词；它描述的是一种法律状态，而不是动作。

entries.definition: From Latin punire with an adjective suffix; it describes the purpose of a measure rather than the deed itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 punire 加形容词后缀而来；它描述一项措施的目的，而不是行为本身。

entries.definition: Weak and small; it merely looks like punish at the start and is not related to it in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 瘦小虚弱的；只是开头与 punish 相似，并非同源。

entries.definition: To impose a penalty, usually under a written rule; it stresses the rule, while punish stresses the suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 通常依据成文规则施加处罚；它强调规则，而 punish 强调痛苦。

entries.definition: To correct behaviour through training or punishment; reform is the aim, which punish does not imply.
entries.definitionCN: 通过训练或惩罚纠正行为；改正是目的，punish 并不含此意。

entries.definition: To punish or scold severely; it often means words rather than physical suffering and sounds formal.
entries.definitionCN: 严厉惩罚或斥责；常指言语而非肉体痛苦，语体正式。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'relating to punishment'; it cannot take an object and never names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与刑罚有关的」形容词；它不能带宾语，也不指动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real derived family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的派生词族与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Punish goes back through French punir to Latin punire, and behind punire stands poena, the price of a wrong.
normal.cn: punish 经法语 punir 上溯拉丁 punire，而 punire 背后站着 poena，即过错的代价。

normal.en: The family keeps splitting the same idea: punishment is the suffering, punitive is the intention, punishable is the liability.
normal.cn: 这一词族不断拆分同一个观念：punishment 是那份痛苦，punitive 是那种意图，punishable 是那种责任。

normal.en: Punish almost always asks two questions: who suffers, and for what.
normal.cn: punish 几乎总要回答两个问题：谁受苦，以及为了什么。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the legal core: punish offenders, punish wrongdoing, be punished by law.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出法律内核：惩罚违法者、惩处不当行为、受法律制裁。

normal.en: The object can be a person, a body, a pair of shoes or an opponent, but the verb always means someone or something pays.
normal.cn: 宾语可以是人、身体、一双鞋或一个对手，但这个动词始终表示「有人或某物在偿付」。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the wrong sits on one pan and the suffering is poured onto the other until the beam levels.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一端放着过错，另一端被倒进痛苦，直到横梁齐平。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt handed to someone who never asked to buy anything.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据被递给一个根本没打算买东西的人。

abstract.en: Picture a path of sharp stones laid across a field so that every step costs the walker something.
abstract.cn: 想象田野上铺着一条尖石小路，每走一步都要让行人付出点代价。

examples.en: The school punished the boys for vandalising the gym.
examples.cn: 学校因这些男孩破坏体育馆而惩罚了他们。

examples.en: Years of heavy loads had punished the truck's suspension.
examples.cn: 多年的重载已经把卡车的悬挂系统损耗得很厉害。

examples.en: The home side punished every mistake in the second half.
examples.cn: 主队在下半场抓住了每一次失误并加以重创。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕你失」——怕你失了规矩，就先让你吃一阵苦头 → 惩罚、处罚

root: 希腊 poine「为过错付出的价」→ 拉丁 poena「罚、补偿」→ 拉丁动词 poenire / punire「施罚、索偿」→ 古法语 punir → 英语 punish；同族词有 punishment、punishable、punitive、penal、penalty。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: a wrong creates a debt, and suffering collects it. The collection can be a general punishment, a court sentence, a parent's correction, deliberate harshness, wear on an object, a heavy defeat, sharp criticism, or plain physical exhaustion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一条线展开：过错生出一笔债，而痛苦负责把它收回。收回的方式可以是泛指的惩罚、法庭的判决、父母的管教、刻意的严酷、对物品的损耗、一场惨败、尖锐的批评，或纯粹的身体消耗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mallet falls and the offender leaves his seat to bear the pain he brought about.
core.cn: 核心意象：木槌落下，犯错的人离开座位，去承受自己招来的那阵疼痛。

branches.en: BASE ACT: pain is deliberately dealt out because a wrong was done.
branches.cn: 基础动作：因为有人做错，痛苦被刻意施加出去。

branches.en: TWO COURTS: the debt is collected by a judge with a sentence, or by a parent with a withdrawn privilege.
branches.cn: 两种法庭：债由法官以判决收取，或由父母以收回特权收取。

branches.en: HARSHNESS WITHOUT A RULE: suffering continues even when no rule existed to be broken.
branches.cn: 无规之严：即便没有可供违反的规则，痛苦仍被继续施加。

branches.en: NON-HUMAN TARGETS: an object wears out under rough use, or an opponent is crushed by a score.
branches.cn: 非人对象：物品在粗暴使用下损耗，对手被比分碾碎。

branches.en: COST WITHOUT A VERDICT: words wound a reputation, and effort wrings out the body.
branches.cn: 无判决的代价：言语损伤名声，用力榨干身体。

intro.en: Punish sits at the head of an English family whose members split the ideas of act, result, liability and purpose.
intro.cn: punish 位于一个英语词族的首位，其成员分别承担动作、结果、责任与目的这几层意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin poena and the verb punire underlie punish, punishment, punishable and punitive, while the adjective poenalis leads to penal and penalty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 poena 与动词 punire 位于 punish、punishment、punishable 与 punitive 之下，而形容词 poenalis 则通向 penal 与 penalty。

items.meaning: to exact a price for a wrong
items.example: The stem appears in several English words.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在好几个英语词里。

items.meaning: to make someone suffer for a wrong
items.example: They punished him for the delay.
items.exampleCN: 他们因延误而惩罚了他。
那是一个折磨人的日程。

items.example: The offence is punishable by fine.
items.exampleCN: 该违法行为可处以罚金。
施罚者很少能免于责难。
他们加征了惩罚性关税。

definition_zh: 惩罚；刑罚；处罚；严厉对待：因过错而施加的痛苦或损失，也指行为主义中用以降低行为频率的后果
definition_en: pain, loss or other hardship imposed for a fault, including the consequence used in behaviourism to make an act less frequent
core_image: 一只伸向热炉的手被烫得立刻缩回，炉子原地未动，退缩的是那只手
scene: 手刚碰到热炉边缘就猛地缩回，炉子原地未动。The punishment was immediate, and the child never reached for the stove again.
sceneCN: 这里指因过错而施加的痛苦后果（第 1 个义项：一般意义上的惩罚）；句意为惩罚来得即时，孩子此后再也没有伸手去碰炉子；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 惩罚；处罚（可数与不可数兼有）
刑罚；体罚（法律或行为主义用法）

forms.label: 复数（指具体处罚种类或次数）

derivatives.zh: punire 去词尾 → 施加惩罚，语义保留「使付出代价」
punire + -ive（具有……性质的）→ 以惩罚为目的的
punish + -able（可……的）→ 可受惩罚的
punish + -ing（现在分词形容词）→ 令人疲惫不堪的，语义偏移为「折磨人的」
in-（不） + poena（惩罚）→ 免受惩罚，词根相同而前缀相反

senses.title: Pain imposed for a fault
senses.titleCN: 因过错而施加的痛苦或损失
senses.definition: something unpleasant imposed on a person because of a wrong or a broken rule
senses.definitionCN: 因错误或违反规则而加在人身上的不快后果
senses.example: The punishment for the prank was a week without a bicycle.
senses.exampleCN: 恶作剧的惩罚是一周不许骑车。
senses.why: Latin poena meant 'penalty, compensation', so punishment begins as a price paid for a wrong.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 poena 意为「罚金、补偿」，惩罚最初就是为过错付出的代价。

senses.title: A legal penalty
senses.definition: a penalty imposed by a court for an offence, such as a fine, imprisonment or loss of rights
senses.definitionCN: 法院对罪行施加的罚金、监禁或剥夺权利等处罚
senses.example: The punishment for the offence was reduced on appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 该项罪行的刑罚在上诉后被减轻。
senses.why: law formalised the payment: the community takes something from the offender in return for the harm.
senses.whyCN: 法律把这种偿付形式化：社群从违法者那里取走某物，以抵偿损害。

senses.title: A penalty under rules
senses.definition: a penalty imposed within a game, school or workplace for breaking its rules
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、学校或工作场所内因违反规则而施加的处罚
senses.example: The referee's punishment was a penalty kick.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判的处罚是一个点球。
senses.why: any rule-governed group needs a price for breaking rules, and the same word covers it.
senses.whyCN: 任何受规则约束的群体都需要为违规定一个代价，同一个词便覆盖了它。

senses.title: Harsh treatment
senses.definition: rough, exhausting or cruel treatment that goes beyond any stated rule
senses.definitionCN: 超出任何明文规则的粗暴、耗人或不人道对待
senses.example: The old boat took a punishment in every storm.
senses.exampleCN: 这条旧船在每场风暴中都遭到重创。
senses.why: when no rule is stated, the word still names harm inflicted, and it extends to objects and bodies.
senses.whyCN: 没有明文规则时，这个词仍指被施加的伤害，并扩展到物体与身体。

senses.title: The behaviourist consequence
senses.titleCN: 行为主义中降低行为频率的后果
senses.definition: a consequence that makes a behaviour less likely to recur, in contrast with reinforcement
senses.definitionCN: 使行为更不可能再次发生的后果，与强化相对
senses.example: The punishment reduced the number of late arrivals but also raised absenteeism.
senses.exampleCN: 惩罚减少了迟到次数，却也提高了缺勤率。
senses.why: psychology needed the exact opposite of reinforcement, and it reused the everyday word for paying for a wrong.
senses.whyCN: 心理学需要强化的精确对立面，便复用了这个表示「为过错付出代价」的日常词。

senses.title: Corporal punishment
senses.definition: physical punishment such as hitting, used especially of school or household discipline
senses.definitionCN: 殴打等身体惩罚，尤指学校或家庭管教
senses.example: Corporal punishment was banned in the district's schools.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区的学校禁止体罚。
senses.why: the body is the oldest surface on which a penalty is written, so the compound names that case directly.
senses.whyCN: 身体是最古老的书写惩罚的表面，因此这个复合词直接命名那种情形。

senses.title: A financial penalty
senses.definition: a sum of money exacted for a violation, delay or breach of contract
senses.definitionCN: 因违规、延误或违约而被收取的一笔钱
senses.example: The punishment for late filing was a fixed fee.
senses.exampleCN: 逾期申报的处罚是一笔固定费用。
senses.why: poena was originally a payment, so a fine is the most literal modern descendant.
senses.whyCN: poena 原本就是一种付款，因此罚款是这个词最字面的现代后裔。

senses.title: Self-punishment
senses.definition: harm a person inflicts on themselves out of guilt, shame or a sense of owed payment
senses.definitionCN: 出于内疚、羞耻或「应当偿付」之感而对自己施加的伤害
senses.example: His punishment was to give up the thing he loved most.
senses.exampleCN: 他的自我惩罚是放弃自己最爱的东西。
senses.why: if a wrong creates a debt, the debtor can be both the one who owes and the one who collects.
senses.whyCN: 如果过错产生债务，欠债者与收债者可以是同一个人。

intro.en: Punishment comes from Latin poena 'penalty, compensation' through the verb punire and Old French. The ultimate source is Greek poine 'penalty, recompense'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: punishment 经动词 punire 与古法语上溯拉丁 poena「罚金、补偿」。其最终来源是希腊 poine「惩罚、报偿」。年代为约数。

items.en: Poine meant 'penalty, recompense, blood-money'. The idea is payment for a wrong rather than correction of the offender.
items.cn: poine 意为「惩罚、报偿、血金」。其观念是为过错付款，而不是矫正犯错者。

items.en: Latin poena meant 'penalty, punishment, compensation'. It is the source of penal, penalty and impunity as well.
items.cn: 拉丁 poena 意为「罚金、惩罚、补偿」。它也是 penal、penalty 与 impunity 的来源。

items.en: Punire meant 'to punish, to avenge, to take vengeance for'. Its noun punitio named the act of punishing.
items.cn: punire 意为「惩罚、报仇、为……复仇」。其名词 punitio 指惩罚行为。

items.en: Old French punir and punissement carried the legal sense into English from the twelfth century onward.
items.cn: 古法语 punir 与 punissement 从 12 世纪起把法律义带入英语。

items.en: English punishment covered both the legal penalty and the general infliction of pain, and later the rough wear that objects endure.
items.cn: 英语 punishment 兼指法律刑罚与一般施加的痛苦，后来又指物体承受的粗暴损耗。

items.en: Reconstructed form (pre-Greek root): poine is often attached to an Indo-European root for 'payment, price', but that root is a reconstruction and no single pre-Greek form is demonstrated; the Greek noun itself is attested.
items.cn: 重构形式（希腊语之前的词根）：poine 常被挂到印欧语「付款、价格」词根上，但该词根属重构，也没有单一的前希腊语形式得到证明；这个希腊名词本身有书证。

note.en: Group one holds legal and formal relatives that are easily confused with the general word; group two holds other imposed consequences with a different purpose.
note.cn: 第一组是易与通称混淆的法律与正式同族词；第二组是目的不同的其他施加性后果。

entries.definition: The specific disadvantage attached to a rule or offence, such as a fine; punishment is the wider act or institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则或罪行所附的具体不利后果，如罚款；punishment 是更宽的行为或制度。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'intended to punish'; it describes the aim of a measure, not the measure itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「以惩罚为目的」的形容词，描述措施的目的，而非措施本身。

entries.definition: Exemption from punishment, built with a negative prefix on the same Latin root; it is the opposite condition.
entries.definitionCN: 免受惩罚，在同一拉丁词根上加否定前缀，指相反的状态。

entries.definition: A penalty imposed by an authority or by states; it is formal and often collective, while punishment can be personal.
entries.definitionCN: 由权威或国家施加的处罚，正式且常为集体性；punishment 可以是个人性的。

entries.definition: Punishment understood as deserved payback; it stresses the balance of harm rather than the rule broken.
entries.definitionCN: 被理解为应得报偿的惩罚，强调伤害的平衡，而非被违反的规则。

entries.definition: Any result of an act, pleasant or not; it carries no judgment, whereas punishment implies a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 任何行为的结果，好坏皆可，不带评判；punishment 则含有过错之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real legal collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实法律搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: poena 'price paid': punishment is a price exacted for a wrong.
normal.cn: poena「付出的价钱」：惩罚就是为过错索取的价钱。

normal.en: The family runs punish, punishment, punitive, punishable, impunity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 punish、punishment、punitive、punishable、impunity。

normal.en: Legal phrases pin the formal sense: capital punishment, corporal punishment, impose a punishment.
normal.cn: 法律搭配钉住正式义：死刑、体罚、施加惩罚。

normal.en: The prefix in impunity is negative, so impunity is the absence of the price.
normal.cn: impunity 里的前缀是否定的，因此 impunity 就是没有这笔价钱。

normal.en: The behaviourist pair is punishment and reward, moving frequency down and up.
normal.cn: 行为主义的配对是惩罚与奖励，分别把频率往下与往上推。

abstract.en: Picture a hand touching a hot stove and pulling back at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手碰到热炉，立刻缩回。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt handed over for a debt nobody wanted to pay.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据，为一笔没人想付的债开出。

abstract.en: Picture a judge and an offender both holding the same coin.
abstract.cn: 想象法官与犯错者同时握着同一枚硬币。

examples.en: The punishment must fit the offence, the old principle runs.
examples.cn: 古老的原则说，惩罚必须与罪行相称。

examples.en: Punishment alone rarely teaches the behaviour that should replace it.
examples.cn: 单靠惩罚很少能教会被替代的正确行为。

examples.en: The fine was a punishment for late payment, not a fee for service.
examples.cn: 这笔罚款是对迟付的惩罚，而非服务费。

dict_mnemonic.text: punish（惩罚）+ ment（名词）＝ 惩罚；记「手碰热炉，缩回的是手」。

root: 希腊 poine「惩罚、报偿」→ 拉丁 poena「罚金、补偿」→ punire「惩罚」→ 古法语 punir／punissement。poine 的希腊语之前来源不确定，与印欧语「付款、价格」词根的联系属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one price: a wrong creates a debt, the court collects it, a rule collects it, a body pays it, and psychology and conscience each keep a ledger.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一笔价钱展开：过错产生一笔债，法庭来收，规则来收，身体来付，心理学与良心各自记着一本账。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand touches a hot stove, withdraws at once, and the stove has not moved.
core.cn: 核心意象：手碰到热炉，立刻缩回，炉子却原地未动。

branches.en: THE PRICE: a fault creates something owed, and punishment is the payment demanded.
branches.cn: 价钱：过错产生应偿之物，惩罚就是被索取的偿付。

branches.en: TWO COLLECTORS: a court and a rule-governed group both exact the price.
branches.cn: 两个收取者：法庭与受规则约束的群体都来收取这笔价钱。

branches.en: THE BODY: rough treatment and corporal discipline write the penalty on a body.
branches.cn: 身体：粗暴对待与体罚把惩罚写在身体上。

branches.en: TWO LEDGERS: behaviourism lowers frequency, and a fine lowers the bank balance.
branches.cn: 两本账：行为主义降低频率，罚款降低账户余额。

branches.en: THE SELF: when the debtor and the collector are one person, the punishment turns inward.
branches.cn: 自身：当欠债者与收债者同为一人，惩罚便转向内。

intro.en: Punishment is a Latin root plus an English noun suffix, and the root also builds the legal family of penalty, punitive and impunity.
intro.cn: punishment 是拉丁词根加英语名词后缀，这个词根还构成 penalty、punitive 与 impunity 这一法律词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin poena 'penalty' gives punire 'to punish' and punitio 'punishment'; the English suffix -ment names the act or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 poena「罚金」给出 punire「惩罚」与 punitio「惩罚」；英语后缀 -ment 命名行为或其结果。

items.example: The noun is the root of penalty and impunity too.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词也是 penalty 与 impunity 的词根。

items.structure: punire, punivi, punitum (Latin verb, fourth conjugation)
items.example: The verb carries the idea of collecting a debt.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词带着「收取债务」的意思。

items.example: The action noun is the Latin model behind the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动作名词是英语词背后的拉丁模板。

items.example: The verb is the everyday member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族中最日常的一员。

items.meaning: the act or result of punishing
items.example: The suffix turns the act into a countable thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把行为变成可计数之物。

items.example: The adjective marks purpose rather than act.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记目的，而非行为。

items.example: The suffix marks what the law can reach.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记法律能触及的范围。

items.example: The negative prefix reverses the whole idea.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀把整个观念反过来。

items.meaning: a specific disadvantage for an offence
items.meaningCN: 对过错的具体不利后果
items.example: The word is the countable cousin of punishment.
items.exampleCN: 这个词是 punishment 的可计数近亲。

definition_zh: 学生；瞳孔
definition_en: a child at school, or the dark opening in the centre of the eye
core_image: 教室里一个小学生举手，近看他的眼睛中央有一点黑
scene: 教室里一个小学生举手，眼睛中央那点黑被光照得发亮。The pupil answered the teacher's question.
sceneCN: 这里 pupil 是「学生」（第 01 个义项）；句意是那个学生回答了老师的问题；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 名词：学生、瞳孔

derivatives.zh: 受监护期
瞳孔的

senses.title: A child who is taught at school
senses.definition: A child who is taught at school
senses.definitionCN: 在校读书的孩子
senses.example: The pupil answered the teacher's question.
senses.exampleCN: 那个学生回答了老师的问题。
senses.why: Pupil came from Latin pupillus, a young ward under a guardian, and English kept it for a child in school.
senses.whyCN: pupil 源自拉丁语 pupillus（受监护的未成年人），英语用它指在校的孩子。

senses.title: The dark opening in the centre of the eye
senses.definition: The dark opening in the centre of the eye
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛中央的黑色开口
senses.example: The doctor looked at my pupils in the light.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在灯下看我的瞳孔。
senses.why: Latin pupilla meant the little girl reflected in another's eye; that small dark image gave the eye opening its name.

definition_zh: 购买；购置；购得之物；（以努力或牺牲）取得；紧握；抓握力；杠杆支点；（古）掠夺所得
definition_en: to get something by paying money, or to obtain it by effort; also the firm hold by which power is applied
core_image: 一个人向前追着猎物跑，追上后死死攥住不放——先「追着取得」，很久以后才专指「用钱买下」

sceneCN: 这里 purchase 是「购得之物」（第 3 个义项：已经买到手的东西）；句意：留好小票，这件超过五十美元的购得之物没有它就不能退。画面里有柜台、收据和盖章的手；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 购买；购置；（以努力）取得；紧握

senses.title: To buy: hand over money and take the thing
senses.definition: to get goods, services, or property by paying money for them
senses.definitionCN: 用钱取得货物、服务或财产
senses.example: She purchased a used car for three thousand dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 她花三千美元买了一辆二手车。
senses.why: The verb came from Old French porchacier, pur- 'forth' plus chacier 'to chase': to purchase was to go after something until you had it. Only in the mid-14c. did 'get by paying money' become the dominant sense.
senses.whyCN: 动词来自古法语 porchacier，由 pur-「向前」加 chacier「追逐」构成：purchase 本是「追着去取得」。到 14 世纪中期，「付钱取得」才成为主义。

senses.title: Procurement: the formal act of acquiring
senses.titleCN: 购置：有手续的正式取得
senses.definition: the formal or large-scale act of buying goods, equipment, or property
senses.definitionCN: 正式或大宗地购买货物、设备或财产的行为
senses.example: The university approved the purchase of new laboratory equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 校方批准了购置新的实验室设备。
senses.why: The noun's sense 'act of acquiring, procurement' is recorded from the late 14c. Modern institutions narrowed it to documented buying: the chase is gone, and what remains is a deliberate, recorded acquisition.
senses.whyCN: 名词「取得、采购的行为」记录于 14 世纪后期。现代机构把它收窄为有单据的购买：追逐不见了，剩下的是有步骤、有记录的取得。

senses.title: The thing bought: an object with a receipt
senses.titleCN: 购得之物：带小票的那件东西
senses.definition: something that has been bought
senses.definitionCN: 已经买到手的东西
senses.example: Her most expensive purchase was a second-hand piano.
senses.exampleCN: 她最贵的一件购得之物是一架二手钢琴。
senses.why: 'That which is bought' dates from the 1580s, three centuries after the verb. The older noun meant 'acquisition, booty'; once buying became the main sense, the object bought could inherit the name.
senses.whyCN: 「买到的东西」这一义项始于 16 世纪 80 年代，比动词晚三百年。早先名词指「获得物、战利品」；当购买成为主义，被买下的东西就继承了这个词。

senses.title: To win at a price: obtain by effort or loss
senses.titleCN: 以代价取得：用努力或牺牲换来
senses.definition: to obtain something valuable through effort, suffering, or sacrifice rather than money
senses.definitionCN: 通过努力、受苦或牺牲而得到有价值的东西，而非用钱
senses.example: They purchased their freedom with years of struggle.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用多年的斗争换来了自由。
senses.why: This is the oldest English sense: c.1300 purchase meant 'acquire, obtain, procure' by any means, including merit or suffering. 'To purchase peace with blood' keeps that breadth, where money is only one possible price.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最古老的义项：约 1300 年 purchase 指以任何方式「取得、获得、谋得」，包括功劳或受苦。「以鲜血换取和平」保留了这种宽度，钱只是众多代价之一。

senses.title: A firm grip: the hold that keeps the thing
senses.titleCN: 紧握：攥住不放的那只手
senses.definition: a firm hold or grasp on something, especially one that gives control
senses.definitionCN: 对某物的牢固抓握，尤指带来控制权的握持
senses.example: He got a purchase on the rope and pulled himself up.
senses.exampleCN: 他抓住绳子，把自己拉了上去。
senses.why: The noun sense 'firm hold by which power may be exerted' is from 1711, extended from a nautical verb of the 1560s meaning 'to haul or draw, especially by mechanical power', as sailors purchase an anchor. Gripping and buying share the image of pulling something into your possession.
senses.whyCN: 名词「可以施加力量的牢固把握」始于 1711 年，来自 16 世纪 60 年代一个航海动词「拉、绞（尤用机械力）」，如水手绞起锚。抓握与购买共享同一个意象：把东西拉进自己的掌控。

senses.title: Leverage: the point where a small force wins
senses.titleCN: 杠杆支点：小力撬动大物的那个点
senses.definition: a position or hold that gives mechanical advantage, the point where a lever or force bites
senses.definitionCN: 带来机械优势的位置或着力点，即杠杆或力量咬住的那一点
senses.example: Put the jack under the beam to get a better purchase.
senses.exampleCN: 把千斤顶放到梁下，好取得更好的着力点。
senses.why: Mechanical 'purchase' names the hold or position that lets a small force move a great weight, the same word sailors used for hauling. The point where the lever bites is literally a place to grip.
senses.whyCN: 机械上的 purchase 指让小力移动重物的着力点或握位，正是水手「绞拉」时用的词。杠杆咬住的那一点，字面上就是一个可以握紧的地方。

senses.title: Purchasing: buying turned into a department
senses.titleCN: 采购：变成一门部门工作的购买
senses.definition: the institutional activity or department responsible for buying supplies and equipment
senses.definitionCN: 负责购买物资与设备的机构性活动或部门
senses.example: She works in purchasing, sourcing parts for the whole factory.
senses.exampleCN: 她在采购部工作，为整个工厂寻找零件。
senses.why: In business and government, purchasing became a department and a process in the 20th c.: purchase orders, purchasing agents. The act of buying is institutionalised and separated from the person who pays.
senses.whyCN: 在商业与政府里，purchasing 在 20 世纪成为一个部门和流程：采购订单、采购员。购买行为被制度化，与掏钱的人分开了。

senses.title: To secure title: land and rights, not shopping
senses.titleCN: 置产、买断：买的是产权，不是商品
senses.definition: to acquire property, land, or legal rights by payment, especially on a large or formal scale
senses.definitionCN: 通过付款取得财产、土地或法律权利，尤指大宗或正式的
senses.example: The company purchased the land from the county in 1998.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司于 1998 年从县政府买下了这块土地。
senses.why: Legal and landed use keeps the noun's weight: a purchase of land or of rights is an acquisition of title, not a shopping trip. The word still carries the old sense of getting something permanently into your holdings.
senses.whyCN: 法律与地产用法保留了名词的分量：purchase of land or rights 是取得产权，而不是逛街购物。这个词仍带着「把某物永久纳入自己名下」的旧义。

senses.title: Booty: what was taken before it was bought
senses.titleCN: 掠夺所得：还没「买」之前，是抢来的
senses.definition: in older usage, goods gained by pillage or robbery; spoils
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法：通过掠夺或抢劫得到的财物；战利品
senses.example: In the old chronicle, the raiders divided their purchase among the ships.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部旧编年史里，劫掠者把抢来的财物分给了各条船。
senses.why: The noun's first English sense (c.1300) was 'booty, spoil, goods gained by pillage'; 'to make purchase' once meant 'to seize by robbery'. The polite buyer of today stands where a raider once stood.
senses.whyCN: 名词最早的英语义项（约 1300 年）是「战利品、掠夺所得」；to make purchase 一度意为「抢劫夺取」。今天彬彬有礼的买主，站的是当年劫掠者的位置。

intro.en: Purchase begins as a chase, not a transaction: Old French porchacier meant to go after something and get it. Money entered the word only in the 14th century, and the grip-and-lever senses came from sailors hauling anchors.
intro.cn: purchase 起于追逐而非交易：古法语 porchacier 意为追着去取得。金钱在 14 世纪才进入这个词，而「抓握、杠杆」义来自水手绞锚。

items.en: Porchacier (later pourchasser) meant 'search for, procure; aim at, strive for, pursue eagerly'. It joins pur- 'forth' with chacier 'to run after, hunt, chase' (see chase). The exact force of pur- here, whether 'forward' or an intensive, is uncertain and is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: Porchacier（后作 pourchasser）意为「寻找、谋得、力求、急切追求」，由 pur-「向前」加 chacier「追赶、打猎、追逐」（见 chase）构成。pur- 在此究竟是「向前」还是加强语气，来源不确定，故标为「来源不确定」。

items.en: The Anglo-French verb purchaser meant 'go after' and carried the legal-administrative tone of obtaining something. English took it over as purchase with a very wide meaning.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-法语动词 purchaser 意为「追赶、追求」，并带有取得某物的法律行政语气。英语借用为 purchase，含义非常宽。

items.en: The verb is first recorded as 'acquire, obtain; get, receive; procure, provide', also 'bring about, instigate, contrive'. At this stage money is not required: merit, suffering, or effort can be the price.
items.cn: 动词最早记录为「取得、获得、得到、领受、谋得、提供」，也有「促成、煽动、策划」义。此时并不需要金钱：功劳、受苦或努力都可以是代价。

items.en: The specific sense 'acquire or secure by expenditure of money or its equivalent, pay money for, buy' appears in the mid-14c. The older 'get by conquest in war, obtain as booty' survived into the 17c.
items.cn: 「以金钱或其等价物取得、付钱买下」这一具体义项出现于 14 世纪中期。更早的「以战争征服取得、作为战利品获得」一直用到 17 世纪。

items.en: A nautical verb 'to haul or draw, especially by mechanical power' (1560s, used of hauling up anchors) produced the noun sense 'firm hold by which power may be exerted' in 1711. Meanwhile 'that which is bought' is recorded from the 1580s.
items.cn: 航海动词「拉、绞，尤指用机械力」（16 世纪 60 年代，用于绞起锚）在 1711 年衍生出名词「可以施加力量的牢固把握」；同时「买到的东西」记录于 16 世纪 80 年代。

items.en: The noun's journey runs from 'booty, spoil' (c.1300) to 'act of acquiring' (late 14c.) to 'thing bought' (1580s) and finally to the 20th-century department of purchasing. Plunder, transaction, object, institution: one word, four stages.
items.cn: 名词的旅程从「战利品、掠夺物」（约 1300）到「取得行为」（14 世纪后期），再到「买到的东西」（16 世纪 80 年代），最后到 20 世纪的采购部门。劫掠、交易、物品、机构：一个词，四个阶段。
