branches.cn: 同一种深色的围巾与手套

branches.en: walls that look black at night
branches.cn: 夜里几乎像黑色的墙面

branches.en: a robe that only one family could pay for
branches.cn: 只有一家人买得起的袍子

branches.en: a novel dressed up in decoration
branches.cn: 打扮得过分的小说

branches.en: a dye so costly that it named both a colour and a rank
branches.cn: 昂贵到同时命名了颜色与地位的染料

intro.en: A Greek noun for the shellfish and its dye holds the word together, and Latin, Old English and English endings carry it into colour, cloth and style.
intro.cn: 表示贝类及其染料的希腊语名词支撑着这个词，拉丁语、古英语与英语的词形再把它带到颜色、布匹与文风上。

latinIntro.en: Latin purpura, the dye and the cloth, and the verb purpurare, to dye purple, come from Greek porphyra and stand behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 purpura（染料与紫布）与动词 purpurare（染紫）来自希腊语 porphyra，是英语这个词的来源。

items.meaning: the colour, or of that colour

definition_zh: 目的；意图；用途；决心；意义；宗旨
definition_en: the reason for which something is done, made or exists
core_image: 木匠在工作台上把一块木板摆正，用粉线弹出一条笔直的线，才落下第一锯
scene: 开工之前，工头把图纸摊在木板上，用手指按住那条基准线，说明这块料为什么要留厚两毫米。The purpose of the extra thickness was to allow a second plane pass.
sceneCN: 这里 purpose 指「做某件事所依据的目的」（第 1 个义项：意图与目的）；句意为多留那两毫米是为了还能再刨一次。图中可辨识物件：摊开的图纸、按住基准线的手指、弹过粉线的木板、留下的余量；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 目的；意图；用途；决心；意义；宗旨
（较少用）打算；意图

derivatives.zh: 由名词加表示「充满」的形容词后缀构成，语义由「目的」转为「有明确目的的」
由名词加副词后缀构成，语义由「意图」转为「故意地」
加表示「缺少」的形容词后缀构成，语义由「目的」转为「没有目的的」
由名词与过去分词复合而成，语义由「用途」转为「专为某用途建造的」
加表示「多」的前缀构成，语义由「用途」转为「一物多用的」

senses.title: The reason for an act
senses.titleCN: 做一件事的理由与意图
senses.definition: the reason one has in mind for doing something or for making something
senses.definitionCN: 做某事或造某物时心里所抱的理由
senses.example: The purpose of the extra thickness was to allow a second plane pass.
senses.exampleCN: 多留那两毫米，是为了还能再刨一次。
senses.why: the word comes from putting something forward, so a purpose is the aim a person sets in front of the work before starting it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自「把某物摆到前面」，因此目的就是开工前把目标摆在工作前面的那件事。

senses.title: The function of a thing
senses.definition: the job that an object or a part is designed to perform
senses.definitionCN: 一件物件或部件被造出来所要承担的功能
senses.example: This room has outlived its original purpose as a laundry.
senses.exampleCN: 这间屋子原本用作洗衣房，如今那个用途早已过去了。
senses.why: the aim moves from the maker's head into the made thing, where it becomes a function.
senses.whyCN: 目标从造物者的脑子里移到被造之物里，在那里它就成了一种功能。

senses.title: Firmness of intention
senses.definition: resolute determination to carry out what one has decided
senses.definitionCN: 把已经决定的事做到底的那份坚决
senses.example: He spoke with purpose and nobody interrupted.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话带着决心，没人打断。
senses.why: a settled intention shows in the manner of speech, and the noun then names the firmness rather than the aim.
senses.whyCN: 已定的意图会显现在说话的方式上，此时名词指的是那份坚定，而不是目标。

senses.title: Relevance to the matter
senses.definition: the quality of bearing on the question at hand, as in remarks that are to the purpose
senses.definitionCN: 与眼前问题相干的品质，如「切题」的话
senses.example: Every question was to the purpose, and the meeting ended early.
senses.exampleCN: 每个问题都切中正题，会议提前结束。
senses.why: what is aimed at the matter in hand is relevant, so a fixed phrase marks this older, narrower sense.
senses.whyCN: 对准眼前事务的就是相关的，因此一个固定说法保存了这条更窄的旧义。

senses.title: Meaning in a life
senses.definition: the sense that one's existence or work has a point worth serving
senses.definitionCN: 觉得自己的存在或工作有一个值得效力的要点
senses.example: Teaching gave her a purpose she had not found in the laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 教书给了她一种在实验室里没找到的意义。
senses.why: when the aim is large enough to organize a life, the word shifts from a task to a reason for living.
senses.whyCN: 当目标大到足以组织一生，这个词就从一项任务转为活着的理由。

senses.title: A stated aim of an institution
senses.definition: the declared aim that a body, a fund or a law is set up to serve
senses.definitionCN: 一个机构、基金或法律被设立时所声明的目标
senses.example: The fund's purpose is written on its first page.
senses.exampleCN: 这只基金的宗旨写在第一页上。
senses.why: organizations must put their aim forward in writing, which keeps the original image of placing something in front.
senses.whyCN: 机构必须把目标写在前面，这保留了「把某物摆到前面」的原初意象。

senses.title: Result actually achieved
senses.definition: the outcome that an action actually produces, as in efforts that came to good purpose
senses.definitionCN: 一个行动实际产生的效果，如「见了效」的努力
senses.example: All the digging came to good purpose when the well struck water.
senses.exampleCN: 井里出水时，所有挖掘都见了效。
senses.why: an aim that is realized becomes a result, and older English used the noun for that realized effect.
senses.whyCN: 实现的目标会变成结果，旧时英语就用这个名词指那种已实现的效用。

senses.title: A proposal or intent
senses.definition: a plan or proposal one puts forward, the sense closest to the French source
senses.definitionCN: 一个人摆出来的计划或提议，是最贴近法语来源的一层
senses.example: Their purpose was to rebuild the mill before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的打算是在入冬前把磨坊重建起来。
senses.why: the French ancestor meant a proposal put forward, and this plain sense still surfaces in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 法语祖词意为「摆出来的提议」，这一朴素义仍会在正式文字中浮现。

intro.en: Purpose comes through Old French porpos 'aim, intention' from porposer 'to put forth', a variant of proposer, which rests on Latin proponere 'to put forward', built on pro- 'forward' and ponere 'to place'. The deeper origin of ponere is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词经古法语 porpos「目标、意图」来自 porposer「摆出、提出」，那是 proposer 的变体，其源头是拉丁 proponere「放到前面」，由 pro-「向前」与 ponere「放置」构成。ponere 的更深来源尚无定论，年代均为约数。

items.en: Ponere meant 'to put, place, set'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the proposal that links it to a root for 'to place' is circular and adds nothing, so the source is best left open.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放、置、摆」。其更深来源不确定；把它与另一个同样表示「放置」的词根相联系只是循环解释，并无增益，因此来源宜存疑。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ponere gave proponere 'to put forward, set before one', used of plans, terms and proposals.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 ponere 构成 proponere「摆到前面、置于眼前」，用于计划、条款与提议。

items.en: Old French porposer 'to put forth, intend' produced the noun porpos, which named both the aim and the resolve behind it.
items.cn: 古法语 porposer「提出、打算」产生名词 porpos，兼指目标与背后的决心。

items.en: Middle English took purpose for an intention, and the phrase on purpose later fixed the sense of doing something deliberately.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词表示意图，后来固定说法「故意地」把「有意为之」的意思定了下来。

items.en: Modern law and administration use the noun for the declared aim of a body, which is the oldest image of putting an aim in front of the work.
items.cn: 现代法律与行政用这个名词指机构声明的宗旨，这正是「把目标摆在工作前面」最古老的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of ponere and the exact date of the deliberateness phrase): no citation fixes the first use for an institution's aim, and any Indo-European form offered for ponere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（ponere 的更深来源与「故意」说法确切成形的年代）：机构宗旨义没有确切的最早书证；凡为 ponere 给出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates verbs and nouns built on the same placing root; group two separates words for an aim by how explicit it is.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出「放置」词根的动词与名词；第二组按明确程度区分表示「目标」的词。

entries.definition: The direct relative: to put a plan or an offer before others, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 最直接的同族词：把计划或提议摆到别人面前，同出那个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: From the same placing verb through French: to put something forward, hence to set a question or hold a position.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个「放置」动词经法语而来：把某物摆出，因而指提出问题或摆出姿势。

entries.definition: In- 'upon' plus ponere: to place a burden on someone, which is the same root pressing downward.
entries.definitionCN: 由 in-「在上」加 ponere 构成：把负担压在别人身上，同一词根往下用力。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus ponere: to put parts together, hence to write or to calm oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 ponere 构成：把部件放到一起，因而指写作或使镇定。

entries.definition: From pro- plus portare 'to carry': to carry a meaning or a claim, with no placing involved and no shared root.
entries.definitionCN: 由 pro- 加 portare「搬运」构成：承载某种含义或声称，不含「放置」，也不同根。

entries.definition: The thing one intends to hit or reach; it is sharper and more specific than purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 打算击中或抵达的东西；比 purpose 更尖锐、更具体。

entries.definition: A defined end point one can mark and check; purpose is broader and can be a reason rather than a finish line.
entries.definitionCN: 一个可标示、可核对的明确终点；purpose 更宽，可以是理由而非终点线。

entries.definition: What a person means to do, often before acting; it is closer to the mental state than to the thing served.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人打算做什么，多在行动之前；更接近心理状态，而不是所服务的事。

entries.definition: The explanation of why something is as it is; it can look backward, while purpose looks forward.
entries.definitionCN: 解释某事为何如此的理由；可以向后看，而 purpose 向前看。

entries.definition: The work a thing performs; it is the mechanical face of purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 一件东西所执行的工作；是 purpose 在机械层面的面孔。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means to place, and the prefix means forward: a purpose is an aim placed in front of the work.
normal.cn: 词根意为「放置」，前缀意为「向前」：目的就是被摆在工作前面的那个目标。

normal.en: The family runs purpose, purposeful, purposely, purposeless, purpose-built, multipurpose.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖名词、形容词、副词、否定式与两个复合词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: on purpose, serve a purpose, fit for purpose, a sense of purpose.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：故意地、起作用、适合用途、目标感。

normal.en: The siblings propose, pose, impose and compose all come from the same placing verb.
normal.cn: 同族的 propose、pose、impose 与 compose 都出自那个「放置」动词。

normal.en: The look-alike purport comes from a verb meaning to carry, so it means to claim rather than to intend.
normal.cn: 形近的 purport 出自一个意为「搬运」的动词，所以它的意思是「声称」而非「打算」。

abstract.en: Picture a chalk line snapped on a board before the first cut.
abstract.cn: 想象第一锯之前，木板上先弹出的一条粉线。

abstract.en: Picture a sign at the head of a path saying what the path is for.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小路的起点立着一块牌子，写着这条路是为什么修的。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp aimed at one desk rather than lighting the whole room.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯只照一张桌子，而不是照亮整间屋子。

examples.en: The purpose of the new rule is to slow the traffic at the gate.
examples.cn: 新规定的目的是让门口的车辆慢下来。

examples.en: He knocked the cup over on purpose and then apologized.
examples.cn: 他故意碰倒杯子，然后又道了歉。

examples.en: The building has served its purpose and will be pulled down.
examples.cn: 这座楼已经完成它的用途，将被拆除。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「purpose 破的」——先想清楚为什么做，才不容易把事情做破 → 目的

root: 古法语 porpos「目标、意图」← porposer「提出」← 拉丁 proponere「放到前面」= pro-（向前）+ ponere（放置）；ponere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: an aim is placed in front of the work, and that placed aim then becomes a function, a firmness, a relevance, a reason for living, an institutional charter, a realized effect and finally a plain proposal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：先把目标摆到工作前面，这个被摆出的目标随后变成一项功能、一份坚定、一种相关性、一个活着的理由、一纸机构宗旨、一个已实现的效果，最后成为一句朴素的提议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a snapped chalk line laid on a board before the saw goes in.
core.cn: 核心意象：锯子落下之前，先在被板上弹出一条粉线。

branches.en: THE AIM PUT FORWARD: an intention in the mind and a proposal spoken aloud.
branches.cn: 摆出的目标：心里的意图与说出口的提议。

branches.en: THE AIM BUILT IN: one aim settles into a thing's function, another into a body's charter.
branches.cn: 被造进去的目标：一个目标落成物的功能，另一个落成机构的宗旨。

branches.en: THE AIM HELD TIGHT: resolve is the same aim felt as will.
branches.cn: 被握紧的目标：决心就是同一个目标在意志层面的感受。

branches.en: AIMED AND REALIZED: what bears on the matter, and what actually comes of it.
branches.cn: 对准与实现：切中事务的，以及确实做出来的效果。

branches.en: AIM LARGE ENOUGH FOR A LIFE: the aim becomes a reason to get up.
branches.cn: 大到足够撑起一生的目标：目标变成起床的理由。

intro.en: Purpose is a French-shaped noun whose Latin prefix and verb are still productive in English, so its parts can be read clearly.
intro.cn: 这个词是法语形态的名词，其拉丁前缀与动词在英语里仍有构成力，因此部件读得很清楚。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere 'to place' gives propose, impose, compose, position and deposit; pro- 'forward' appears in proceed, promote and protect.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ponere「放置」衍生出 propose、impose、compose、position 与 deposit；pro-「向前」见于 proceed、promote 与 protect。

items.example: The prefix puts the aim ahead of the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把目标放在行动之前。
这个词根提供「放置」的动作。

items.example: The plan was put forward at the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 计划在会上被提了出来。

items.example: The purpose was written on the first page.
A purposeful walk covered the ridge by noon.
items.exampleCN: 一次有目的的行走在正午前走完了山脊。

items.example: She purposely left the door open.

items.exampleCN: 没有目的的挖掘毁了草坪。

items.example: A purpose-built studio replaced the shed.
items.exampleCN: 一间专用工作室取代了棚屋。

items.example: A multipurpose hall serves the whole village.
items.exampleCN: 一座多用途大厅供全村使用。
他们提出了一条更短的路线。

definition_zh: 钱包；女式手袋；财力；资金；奖金
definition_en: a small bag used for carrying money, especially a woman's handbag; also the money a person or group has available, or the prize money offered in a competition
core_image: 围裙内袋里一只磨旧的皮钱袋，装着一整天的收入
scene: 早市快收摊时，卖菜的女人把零钱一张张理平，塞进围裙内侧的布袋。She kept the day's takings in a worn leather purse.
sceneCN: 这里 purse 是「钱包、随身钱袋」（第 1 个义项：装钱的小包）；句意为她把一天的收入放进一只磨旧的皮钱包里。画面里可留意：围裙、理平的零钱、旧皮袋。

pos.zh: 钱包；女式手袋；财力；资金；奖金

derivatives.zh: purse 加表人后缀 -er，原指管钱袋的人，现指船上掌管账目与薪水的职务
cut 与 purse 复合，字面是「割钱袋的人」，指旧时的扒手
purse 与 proud 复合，指因富有而傲慢的

senses.title: A small bag for carrying money
senses.definition: a small bag, often with a clasp, used especially by women for carrying money and a few personal items
senses.definitionCN: 尤指女性使用、常带扣合的小包，用来装钱和少量随身物品
senses.example: She took a coin from her purse and paid the driver.
senses.exampleCN: 她从钱包里取出一枚硬币付给司机。
senses.why: The Latin word behind it named a leather bag, and the first English purses were soft pouches pulled shut with strings, long before notes and cards existed.
senses.whyCN: 它背后的拉丁词本指皮袋，英语最早的 purse 就是用细绳收口的小软袋，那时还没有纸币和银行卡。

senses.title: The money a person or group can spend
senses.definition: the amount of money that a person, family or organization has available to spend
senses.definitionCN: 个人、家庭或机构手头可供支配的钱
senses.example: The repair cost more than the family purse could bear.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔修缮费超出了这个家庭的财力。
senses.why: Once a container holds money, the container can stand for the contents, and then for the spending power those contents give.
senses.whyCN: 容器一旦装着钱，就能代指里面的钱，再进一步指这些钱带来的购买力。

senses.title: Prize money in a competition
senses.definition: the sum of money offered as a prize in a race, a fight or another contest
senses.definitionCN: 赛跑、拳赛或其他比赛中作为奖品的钱
senses.example: The boxer gave his purse to the village school.
senses.exampleCN: 这名拳手把奖金捐给了村里的学校。
senses.why: Prize money was once handed over in an actual bag at the end of a contest, so the name of the container stayed on the prize after payments moved to cheques.
senses.whyCN: 比赛结束时奖金真的装在一只袋子里当场交付，所以即使后来改用支票，容器之名仍留在奖金上。

intro.en: Purse travels back through Old French and medieval Latin to Latin bursa, a leather bag; the Greek word behind bursa is generally thought to be a borrowing, so anything deeper is uncertain.
intro.cn: purse 经古法语与中世纪拉丁语上溯到拉丁语 bursa（皮袋）；bursa 背后的希腊词一般认为也是借词，再往前的来源并不确定。

items.en: Greek byrsa meant a hide or a leather bag, and it is generally considered a loanword into Greek rather than an inherited item.
items.cn: 希腊语 byrsa 指兽皮或皮袋，一般认为它是借入希腊语的词，而非本土传承。

items.en: Latin bursa named a leather pouch and later a treasury or money chest, which is why the family also touches public money.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bursa 指皮制小袋，后来也指金库、钱柜，所以这个词族也涉及公共资金。

items.en: Medieval Latin kept bursa for a bag and a treasury, while Old French developed borse, the form that carried the word towards England.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语保留 bursa 指袋子和金库，古法语则发展出 borse，正是把这个词带向英格兰的形式。

items.en: Middle English purs named a small drawstring pouch worn at the belt, carried by men as well as women.
items.cn: 中古英语 purs 指系在腰带上、用细绳收口的小袋，男女都常佩带。

items.en: Everyday modern English narrows the object to a woman's handbag, while the older sense of available money survives in public purse and purse strings.
items.cn: 现代英语日常用法把这个物件收窄为女式手袋，而「可用之钱」的旧义仍活在 public purse 与 purse strings 里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects spellings and relatives built on the same bag word; the near-meaning group collects other words for what holds money or for money itself.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「袋」词上的拼写与同族词；近义组收其他表示装钱的物件或钱本身的词。

entries.definition: To follow someone in order to catch them; only the opening letters are similar.
entries.definitionCN: 追赶、追求；只是开头几个字母相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The officer on a ship who keeps the accounts and pays the crew.
entries.definitionCN: 船上负责账目与发放薪水的职务。

entries.definition: An official who manages money in a college or school.
entries.definitionCN: 在大学或学校里管理钱财的职务。

entries.definition: To pay money back to someone who has spent it on your behalf.
entries.definitionCN: 把别人替你垫付的钱还给他。

entries.definition: A small flat case for notes and cards, usually carried in a pocket.
entries.definitionCN: 装纸币与卡片的小扁夹，通常放在口袋里。

entries.definition: A bag for personal items, carried especially by women.
entries.definitionCN: 装随身物品的包，尤指女性提包。

entries.definition: Money set aside for a particular purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为某个用途准备的钱。

entries.definition: A shared sum of money collected from a group.
entries.definitionCN: 一群人凑起来共用的一笔钱。

normalIntro.en: The word goes back to a leather bag, and every later sense still keeps something of that one small container.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词源自一只皮袋，后来每个义项都还留着那只小容器的影子。

normal.en: Bursa in Latin is a leather pouch, and the earliest English purses were exactly that: soft bags closed with string.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 bursa 是皮制小袋，英语最早的 purse 正是这种用细绳收口的软袋。

normal.en: Purser keeps the money-handling side of the family: the person on a ship who looks after accounts and pay.
normal.cn: purser 保留了词族中「管钱」的一面：船上负责账目与薪水的人。

normal.en: Reimburse puts re- (back) with a stem from bursa, so the word pictures money going back into the bag it came from.
normal.cn: reimburse 把表示「回」的 re- 与 bursa 的词干结合，画面就是钱回到原来的袋子里。

normal.en: Purse strings were once literal cords; holding them now means controlling the money itself.
normal.cn: purse strings 从前是实实在在的绳子，如今握住它就等于掌控钱财。

normal.en: The public purse treats a whole country's funds as one bag that officials must open with care.
normal.cn: public purse 把一个国家的资金看成一只袋子，官员打开它时必须谨慎。

abstract.en: A purse fits in one hand, yet it can stand for everything a household is able to choose.
abstract.cn: 钱袋一只手就握得住，却可以代表一个家庭所能做的一切选择。

abstract.en: One word names the bag, the money and the prize, because each is something handed from one person to another.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指袋子、又指钱和奖金，因为这三样都是从一个人手里交到另一个人手里。

abstract.en: A purse is often closed not by its clasp but by the fear behind it.
abstract.cn: 钱袋往往是靠背后的顾虑合上的，而不是靠那道扣子。

examples.en: She paid the fare from a small purse she kept in her coat.
examples.cn: 她用外套里一只小钱包付了车费。

examples.en: The tour was cancelled because the club's purse was empty.
examples.cn: 巡演取消了，因为俱乐部的资金已经见底。

examples.en: The winner took home a purse of fifty thousand dollars.
examples.cn: 冠军拿走了五万美元奖金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「珀斯」——去澳大利亚的珀斯旅行，得先备好钱包，记住 purse 是钱包、财力。

root: 拉丁语 bursa（皮袋、钱袋）经中世纪拉丁语与古法语进入中古英语作 purs；同族词多与袋、钱、偿付有关，如 purser、reimburse。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bag that holds money; the senses divide into the bag itself, the money inside it, and the prize once handed over in such a bag.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是装钱的袋子；义项由此分为袋子本身、袋里的钱，以及从前装在这种袋子里交付的奖金。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn leather pouch tucked inside an apron, holding a whole day's earnings.
core.cn: 核心意象：围裙内侧一只磨旧的皮袋，装着一整天的收入。

branches.en: a drawstring pouch on a market stall
branches.cn: 集市摊前一只收口的钱袋

branches.en: a bag whose weight equals a family's choices
branches.cn: 一只袋子的分量等于一个家庭的选择

branches.en: a council counting what it can afford
branches.cn: 市政会算着手里的钱够做什么

branches.en: a prize handed over in a leather bag
branches.cn: 装在皮袋里当场交付的奖金

branches.en: money that is both kept and awarded
branches.cn: 既被存着又被颁出去的同一笔钱

intro.en: The word is held together by a Greek bag word, its Latin descendant, the English noun, and the suffixes that build a person and a paying-back verb.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语的「袋」、它的拉丁后裔、英语名词，以及构成「人」与「偿付」的后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a leather pouch, later a treasury
an officer who handles money on a ship
the cords once used to close a bag

latinEntries.meaning: one who keeps a purse or treasury

definition_zh: 追求；追捕；从事；继续进行；起诉；追随；探究；（对某人）热烈追求
definition_en: to follow someone or something closely, whether to catch it, to continue it, or to win it
core_image: 一个人紧贴着目标的后背跑，目标不停，他也不停——追捕、追梦、追案，都是同一条跑道
scene: 侦探望着巷子尽头，决定一直查到线索断掉为止。We will pursue this case until the last lead runs out.
sceneCN: 这里 pursue 是「继续办理、坚持追查」（第 4 个义项：把事情一路跟到底）；句意：我们会一直追查这个案子，直到最后一条线索用完。画面里有雨巷、手电和翻开的卷宗；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 追求；追捕；从事；继续；起诉；追随

derivatives.zh: 追赶；追求；事务
追赶者；追求者
追赶的；持续追求的
依据……的；按照……的
进行；遵循；从事

senses.title: To go after a goal: keep running toward it
senses.titleCN: 追求目标：一直朝着它跑
senses.definition: to try to achieve something over time, especially a goal, dream, or interest
senses.definitionCN: 长期努力实现某事，尤指目标、梦想或兴趣
senses.example: She moved to Berlin to pursue a career in music.
senses.exampleCN: 她搬到柏林去追求音乐事业。
senses.why: The 'seek, seek to obtain' sense is recorded in English in the late 14c. and was already present in Latin prosequi. A goal is treated as something ahead of you that you follow until you reach it, which is why the verb suits ambitions rather than wishes.
senses.whyCN: 「寻求、力求获得」这一义项在 14 世纪后期见于英语，拉丁语 prosequi 已有此义。目标被当成前方一个可以一路跟随、直到抵达的东西，所以这个词适合形容抱负，而不只是愿望。

senses.title: To chase down: follow with hostile intent
senses.titleCN: 追捕：带着敌意紧跟不放
senses.definition: to follow someone in order to catch or attack them
senses.definitionCN: 紧跟某人以抓住或攻击他
senses.example: Police pursued the stolen van through the narrow streets.
senses.exampleCN: 警察在窄巷里追捕那辆被盗的面包车。
senses.why: This is the word's first English sense (late 13c.): 'follow with hostile intent, follow with a view of overtaking'. The Latin ancestor prosequi meant 'follow after, escort', and hostile pursuit is that following turned aggressive.
senses.whyCN: 这是 pursue 最早的英语义项（13 世纪后期）：「带敌意跟随，意在赶上」。拉丁语祖先 prosequi 意为「跟随、护送」，敌意一起，跟随就变成了追捕。

senses.title: To practise: follow a trade or a subject
senses.titleCN: 从事：把一门职业或学问一路做下去
senses.definition: to engage in an activity, profession, or course of study over a period
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内从事某种活动、职业或学业
senses.example: He pursued medicine for twelve years before changing fields.
senses.exampleCN: 他从医十二年，之后才转行。
senses.why: A career or a subject is something you follow along a track rather than seize once. From 'seek to obtain' the verb widened to 'carry on with', and English says pursue medicine the way it says follow a path.
senses.whyCN: 职业或学问是沿着一条轨道跟随的东西，而不是一下子抓住的东西。动词从「力求获得」扩展到「持续进行」，所以英语说 pursue medicine，就像说 follow a path。

senses.title: To carry on: keep a course of action alive
senses.titleCN: 继续：把一件正在做的事做到底
senses.definition: to continue with an activity, plan, or course of action
senses.definitionCN: 继续进行某项活动、计划或行动方针
senses.example: The committee will pursue the investigation despite the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管有延误，委员会仍将继续这项调查。
senses.why: 'To proceed, to follow (a path), usually figurative' is recorded from the late 14c., and the sense was already in Latin. Continuing is following without stopping: the route stays, you just keep walking it.
senses.whyCN: 「继续进行、沿着（一条路）走，通常为比喻用法」记录于 14 世纪后期，拉丁语已有此义。继续就是不停步地跟随：路线不变，你只管一直走。

senses.title: To sue: follow a case into court
senses.titleCN: 起诉：把案子一路跟进法庭
senses.definition: to take legal action over a claim or wrong, to follow a case through the courts
senses.definitionCN: 就某项请求或过错采取法律行动，把案子跟到法庭
senses.example: The tenant pursued the landlord for the return of the deposit.
senses.exampleCN: 房客起诉房东，要求退还押金。
senses.why: Legal English says pursue a claim much as it says prosecute: Latin prosequi already meant 'follow up, pursue' and gave both words. A lawsuit is a trail you follow to its end, and the court is where the trail stops.
senses.whyCN: 法律英语说 pursue a claim，与说 prosecute 同理：拉丁语 prosequi 本有「跟进、追究」义，两个词都由此而来。诉讼就是一条跟到底的路线，法庭是这条路线的终点。

senses.title: To accompany: follow as an escort
senses.titleCN: 追随、随行：作为随从跟在后头
senses.definition: to follow or accompany someone, especially in order to attend or escort them
senses.definitionCN: 跟随或陪伴某人，尤指为了随侍或护送
senses.example: A small guard pursued the king along the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一小队卫兵沿路跟随国王。
senses.why: Latin prosequi meant 'follow, accompany, attend; follow after, escort', a neutral sense of being behind someone. English kept mostly the aggressive and goal-seeking branches, but the escort sense survives in the Latin-shaped doubling with prosecute and in formal prose.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 prosequi 意为「跟随、陪伴、随侍；跟随、护送」，是「跟在某人后面」的中性义。英语主要保留了攻击性与求取的两支，但「随行」义仍活在 prosecute 等拉丁形同源词和正式文体里。

senses.title: To dig into: follow a question to its source
senses.titleCN: 探究：顺着问题一路挖到源头
senses.definition: to investigate or examine something further, following a line of inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 进一步调查或研究某事物，沿着一条探究线索走
senses.example: The researchers pursued the anomaly until they found its cause.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者一路追查这个异常现象，直到找到原因。
senses.why: An inquiry is a trail: each answer opens the next step. The 'follow' core makes pursue the natural verb for research, where you do not stop at the first clue but keep behind the question.
senses.whyCN: 探究是一条线索：每个答案都打开下一步。「跟随」这个核心让 pursue 成为研究中的自然动词：你不在第一条线索处停下，而是始终坠在问题后面。

senses.title: To court: chase a person, not a thing
senses.titleCN: 追求某人：追的不是事物，是人
senses.definition: to try persistently to win someone's romantic interest
senses.definitionCN: 坚持不懈地争取某人的爱慕
senses.example: He pursued her for months before she agreed to a coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 他追了她好几个月，她才答应喝杯咖啡。
senses.why: The modern romantic sense simply moves the chase from goals and suspects to people. The old hostility is gone, but the structure is identical: someone ahead, you behind, refusing to stop.
senses.whyCN: 现代「追求某人」只是把追逐的对象从目标、嫌疑人换成了人。旧的敌意消失了，结构却一模一样：她在前，你在后，不肯停。

senses.title: To walk a path: follow a route or policy
senses.titleCN: 遵循路径：沿着一条路或方针走
senses.definition: to follow a path, route, or policy, often figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 沿着一条道路、路线或方针前进，常为比喻用法
senses.example: The country pursued a policy of neutrality for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家奉行中立政策数十年。
senses.why: The literal 'follow a path' sense is old and was already figurative in Latin for a course of action. A policy is a road: pursue it and you stay on it, which is why the verb means both 'walk along' and 'carry out'.
senses.whyCN: 「沿着一条路走」的实指义很古老，在拉丁语里已用于比喻「行动方针」。政策就是一条路：pursue 它就是走在上面，所以这个词既表「沿着走」，也表「奉行」。

intro.en: Pursue is built from pro- 'forward' and sequi 'to follow'. Its history runs from Latin escorting, through French chasing, to English ambition, litigation, and research — one verb for every kind of following.
intro.cn: pursue 由 pro-「向前」与 sequi「跟随」构成。它的历史从拉丁语的「随行护送」，经法语的「追赶」，走到英语里的抱负、诉讼与研究——一个动词包揽了所有「跟随」。

items.en: Prosequi meant 'follow, accompany, attend; follow after, escort; follow up, pursue'. It is pro- 'forward' plus sequi 'to follow'. The deeper PIE root *sekw- 'to follow' is a reconstruction with no written record, so that layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: Prosequi 意为「跟随、陪伴、随侍；跟随、护送；跟进、追究」，由 pro-「向前」加 sequi「跟随」构成。更深的印欧语词根 *sekw-「跟随」是重构形式、没有书面记录，因此那一层标为「来源不确定」。

items.en: Spoken Latin reshaped the verb into *prosequare, the form behind the French family. The exact date and region of this reshaping are not recorded, so the timing is source uncertain.
items.cn: 口语拉丁语把这个动词改造成 *prosequare，法语词族即由此而来。这一改造的确切年代与地区没有记录，因此时间标为「来源不确定」。

items.en: Poursuir, with the variant porsivre, meant 'to chase, pursue, follow; continue, carry on'. The two strands English later separated — chasing and continuing — were already together in French.
items.cn: Poursuir（变体 porsivre）意为「追赶、追求、跟随；继续、进行」。英语后来分开的两条线——追捕与继续——在法语里已经并存。

items.en: Anglo-French pursuer and the English verb appear as 'follow with hostile intent, follow with a view of overtaking'. This is the hunting sense that still dominates police reports.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-法语 pursuer 与英语动词出现时意为「带敌意跟随，意在赶上」。这就是至今主导警情报道的追捕义。

items.en: Two quieter senses join: 'to proceed, to follow (a path)', usually figurative for a course of action, and 'to seek, seek to obtain'. Both were already Latin, so English did not invent them; it simply kept more of the parent verb.
items.cn: 两个更安静的义项加入：「继续进行、沿着（一条路）走」（通常比喻行动方针）与「寻求、力求获得」。两者拉丁语已有，英语并非自创，只是保留了母词更多的义项。

items.en: Legal 'pursue a claim' follows the same 'follow it to the end' image, and the 20c. romantic 'pursue someone' moves the chase to people. No new source is involved: both are the old following verb applied to new objects.
items.cn: 法律用语 pursue a claim 沿用的是同一个「一路跟到底」的意象；20 世纪「追求某人」把追逐对象换成了人。两者都没有新词源，只是那个古老的「跟随」动词用在了新对象上。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the act of chasing or striving. It is the noun built on pursue, so the resemblance is real.
entries.definitionCN: 追赶；追求。它是 pursue 衍生出的名词，形似是真的。

entries.definition: done in accordance with something, as in pursuant to the rules. It keeps the French participle shape.
entries.definitionCN: 依据……的；按照……的（pursuant to the rules）。它保留了法语分词形态。

entries.definition: to read through carefully. It resembles pursue but comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 细读。它形似 pursue，但词源不同。

entries.definition: a small bag for money. It shares the opening pur- and nothing else.
entries.definitionCN: 钱包。它只与 pursue 共享开头的 pur-，别无关联。

entries.definition: to run after someone or something in order to catch it. It is the plain, physical word.
entries.definitionCN: 追赶；追逐。它是最朴素、最实指的对应词。

entries.definition: to go or come after someone. It lacks the urgency and hostility of pursue.
entries.definitionCN: 跟随。它没有 pursue 那种急迫与敌意。

entries.definition: to try to find or obtain something. It matches the goal sense but not the chasing.
entries.definitionCN: 寻找；寻求。它对应目标义，但不含追赶。

entries.definition: to conduct a legal case against someone. It is the Latin-shaped twin of pursue in law.
entries.definitionCN: 起诉；检控。它是 pursue 在法律领域的拉丁形姐妹词。

entries.definition: to chase game or search for something persistently. It stresses effort and prey.
entries.definitionCN: 打猎；搜寻。它强调用力与猎物。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin sequi 'to follow', prosequi 'follow after', and the English family pursuit, pursuant, prosecute.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 sequi「跟随」、prosequi「跟随、追究」，以及英语词族 pursuit、pursuant、prosecute。

normal.en: pursue = pro- 'forward' + sequi 'follow': follow forward, and keep following.
normal.cn: pursue = pro-「向前」+ sequi「跟随」：向前跟，而且跟到底。

normal.en: The same sequi gives sequence and consecutive: all of them are about one thing after another.
normal.cn: 同一个 sequi 给出 sequence、consecutive：它们讲的都是一个接一个。

normal.en: Pursue and prosecute are twins: the same Latin verb, one French-shaped, one Latin-shaped.
normal.cn: pursue 与 prosecute 是双胞胎：同一个拉丁动词，一个走法语形，一个走拉丁形。

normal.en: A pursuer is literally 'the one behind you', which is why the word works for detectives and suitors alike.
normal.cn: pursuer 字面上就是「你身后那个人」，所以它同时适用于侦探和求爱者。

normal.en: pursuant to the rules means following the rules, with the old participle still visible.
normal.cn: pursuant to the rules 意为「依据规则」，古老的现在分词仍看得见。

abstract.en: The core is relative position: the target ahead, the pursuer behind, the gap closing or held.
abstract.cn: 核心是相对位置：目标在前，追者在后，距离在缩短或保持。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps the same geometry; only the object changes: a deer, a degree, a lawsuit, a person.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保持同一种几何关系，只换对象：一头鹿、一个学位、一场官司、一个人。

abstract.en: To pursue is never to arrive instantly: the word lives in the interval.
abstract.cn: pursue 从来不是立刻抵达：这个词活在「还没追上」的那段时间里。

examples.en: She decided to pursue a doctorate in linguistics.
examples.cn: 她决定攻读语言学博士学位。

examples.en: The guards pursued the escaped prisoner across the field.
examples.cn: 看守们穿过田野追捕那名逃犯。

examples.en: The company may pursue legal action if the payments stop.
examples.cn: 如果付款停止，公司可能会提起诉讼。

dict_mnemonic.text: per（一直）+ sue（告）——一直跟着、一直告下去 → pursue 追赶、追求、起诉

root: 源自拉丁语 prosequi「跟随、随行、追究」，由 pro-「向前」+ sequi「跟随」构成；经法语 porsivre/poursuir 进入英语，核心始终是「跟在后面、一路不停」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, one geometry: something is ahead of you and you keep after it. Whether it is a suspect, a career, an investigation, a policy, or a person, the verb never changes direction — only what is being followed.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项，一种几何关系：一样东西在你前面，你一路跟着。无论那是嫌疑人、职业、调查、政策还是一个人，这个动词的方向从不改变，变的只是被跟随的对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: staying behind a moving target and refusing to let the gap open.
core.cn: 核心意象：始终坠在一个移动的目标后面，不让距离拉开。

branches.en: THE GOAL AHEAD: ambition, and the inquiry that follows a question to its source.
branches.cn: 前方的目标：抱负，以及顺着问题追到源头的探究。

branches.en: THE LIVING QUARRY: hunting a suspect, and courting a person.
branches.cn: 活的猎物：追捕嫌疑人，以及追求一个人。

branches.en: CARRYING ON: practising a profession, and continuing a course of action.
branches.cn: 持续进行：从事一门职业，以及继续一项行动。

branches.en: THE CASE: following a claim all the way into court.
branches.cn: 案子：把一项请求一路跟进法庭。

branches.en: THE PATH: escorting someone, and walking a route or policy.
branches.cn: 路径：随行护送某人，以及沿一条路线或方针前行。

intro.en: Pursue is pro- plus sequ- plus the French verb ending. Its family shows the prefix pro- 'forward', the root sequ- 'follow', and the suffixes -er, -ant, -ance, and -ing.
intro.cn: pursue 是 pro- 加 sequ- 再加法语动词词尾。它的词族展示前缀 pro-「向前」、词根 sequ-「跟随」，以及后缀 -er、-ant、-ance、-ing。

latinIntro.en: Latin sequi 'to follow' is the base of prosequi 'follow after' and of the English words sequence, consecutive and prosecute. The French branch softened -sequ- into -su-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sequi「跟随」是 prosequi「跟随、追究」的基础，也是英语 sequence、consecutive、prosecute 的基础。法语一支把 -sequ- 软化成了 -su-。

items.meaning: to follow after, whether to catch or to continue
items.meaningCN: 追求；追捕；继续进行（向前跟随）
items.example: He pursued the goal for ten years.
items.exampleCN: 他为这个目标追求了十年。

items.meaning: the act of chasing or striving

items.meaningCN: 追赶者；追求者（-er 施事后缀）
items.example: The pursuer lost the trail in the rain.
items.exampleCN: 追赶者在雨里失去了踪迹。

items.meaningCN: 依据……的；按照……的（-ant 分词后缀）
items.example: Pursuant to the contract, notice must be written.
items.exampleCN: 依据合同，通知必须以书面形式发出。

items.meaning: the carrying out of a plan or duty
items.meaningCN: 进行；履行（-ance 名词后缀）
items.example: He acted in pursuance of his instructions.

items.meaning: to follow up a case in court
items.meaningCN: 起诉；检控（pursue 的拉丁形姐妹词）
items.example: The state prosecuted him for fraud.
items.exampleCN: 州政府以欺诈罪起诉他。

items.structure: Old French suer, from Latin sequi
items.meaning: to take legal action; to follow in court
items.meaningCN: 起诉；诉讼（sequi 的又一后裔）
items.example: She sued the company for damages.
items.exampleCN: 她起诉该公司要求赔偿。

items.structure: Old French suite, from sequi (a following)
items.meaning: a set that follows; a legal case
items.meaningCN: 一套；诉讼（「跟随而来的一组」）
items.example: He filed a suit against his former partner.
items.exampleCN: 他对前合伙人提起了诉讼。

items.meaning: a series of things following one another
items.meaningCN: 顺序；序列（一个接一个跟随）
items.example: Arrange the events in the correct sequence.
items.exampleCN: 按正确顺序排列这些事件。

latinEntries.meaning: to follow, chase (source of French poursuir)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 跟随、追赶（法语 poursuir 的来源，形式为重构）

definition_zh: 推；推动；催促；推销；攻势
definition_en: to press something so that it moves away from you; to urge someone to act; to promote a product or idea; also a strong coordinated effort to achieve something
core_image: 两只手掌抵住一扇沉门，门缝一点点变宽
scene: 货车在坡道上熄了火，司机跳下来，绕到车尾，双手抵住厢板。He pushed hard until the wheels began to turn.
sceneCN: 这里 push 是「用力推」（第 1 个义项：施加力量使物体移动）；句意为他一直用力推，直到车轮开始转动。画面里可留意：货车、坡道、车尾厢板。

pos.zh: 推；推动；催促；推销
推；攻势；努力

derivatives.zh: push 加表人后缀 -er，指推的人，口语中也指贩毒者
push 加 -y 构成形容词，指过分急于达到目的、咄咄逼人的
push 与 up 复合，指靠双臂把身体撑起的俯卧撑
push 与 back 复合，指推回去的力量，现多指反对与抵制

senses.title: To press something away from you
senses.definition: to press a person or thing so that it moves away from you or moves forward
senses.definitionCN: 按住人或物，使它离开你或向前移动
senses.example: He pushed the door open with one shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一边肩膀把门顶开了。
senses.why: The Latin verb behind the word meant to beat or drive, so the earliest English sense is a hand or a body driving an object forward.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁动词本义是击打、驱赶，所以英语最早的义项就是用手或身体把东西向前顶开。

senses.title: To urge someone to act
senses.definition: to urge or pressure someone to do something, especially when they are slow or unwilling
senses.definitionCN: 催促或施压让某人去做某事，尤指对方迟缓或不情愿时
senses.example: The teacher pushed the class to finish before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 老师催全班在中午前做完。
senses.why: A hand can move a thing, and the same force can be applied to a person's will, so physical pressure becomes social pressure.
senses.whyCN: 手能推动物体，同样的力气也能加到人的意愿上，于是身体的推变成了人际的催逼。

senses.title: To promote a product or idea
senses.definition: to try hard to sell a product or to make an idea accepted by many people
senses.definitionCN: 努力卖出产品，或让某个想法被许多人接受
senses.example: The company pushed its new phone through every channel it had.
senses.exampleCN: 公司用尽所有渠道推销它的新手机。
senses.why: Selling is moving goods towards buyers, so the verb for moving an object forward was borrowed for moving goods out of the shop.
senses.whyCN: 销售就是把货物推向买家，于是「把东西往前推」的动词被借来指把货推出店门。

senses.title: A determined campaign or advance
senses.definition: a planned and forceful effort to achieve something, or a military advance
senses.definitionCN: 为达成某事而组织起来的一次有力行动，或军事上的推进
senses.example: The union began a push for shorter hours.
senses.exampleCN: 工会开始了一场争取缩短工时的行动。
senses.why: Beside the verb grew a noun: the whole forward movement, repeated by many hands, became a single campaign with a name.
senses.whyCN: 动词旁边长出了名词：许多人一次次向前使力，整体就成了有名字的一场行动。

intro.en: Push came from Old French pousser, whose Latin ancestor pulsare meant to beat or strike repeatedly; the same Latin family also gave English pulse and compel.
intro.cn: push 来自古法语 pousser，其拉丁语祖先是 pulsare（反复击打）；同一拉丁词族还给英语带来了 pulse 与 compel。

items.en: Pellere meant to drive, strike or set in motion, and it stands behind a large family of Latin verbs of movement.
items.cn: pellere 意为驱动、击打、使动，是拉丁语一大批运动动词的共同源头。

items.en: Pulsare was a frequentative of pellere, meaning to beat or knock again and again, as a hand does on a door.
items.cn: pulsare 是 pellere 的反复动词，意为一下一下地击打，像手在门上敲个不停。

items.en: Old French pousser meant to push or thrust and is the form English borrowed; the older spelling poulser is also recorded.
items.cn: 古法语 pousser 意为推、顶，英语借的正是这个形式；文献中还有更早的拼写 poulser。

items.en: English attests pushen in the thirteenth century, at first for bodily shoving and soon for pressing an argument or a claim.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪已见 pushen，起初指身体上的推搡，很快也用于推进某个论点或主张。

items.en: Modern English extends the verb to advertising, queues, prices and campaigns, while the noun keeps the sense of one coordinated forward movement.
items.cn: 现代英语把动词扩展到广告、排队、价格与竞选，名词则保留「一次协同的向前推进」之意。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the same Latin root of beating and driving; the near-meaning group collects other verbs of moving something by force.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「击打、驱动」词根上的词；近义组收其他表示用力移动某物的动词。

entries.definition: To beat or throb with a regular rhythm.
entries.definitionCN: 有规律地跳动、搏动。

entries.definition: A single beat of the heart or of a regular wave.
entries.definitionCN: 心脏或规律波动的一次搏动。

entries.definition: To force someone to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 迫使某人做某事。

entries.definition: To drive something back or keep it away.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物击退或挡开。

entries.definition: To push someone or something roughly.
entries.definitionCN: 粗暴地推人或推物。

entries.definition: To push gently, often with the elbow.
entries.definitionCN: 轻轻一推，常指用手肘碰。

entries.definition: To drive something forward with sudden force.
entries.definitionCN: 猛地向前推送。

entries.definition: To push steadily against something.
entries.definitionCN: 持续地压、按。

normalIntro.en: The word descends from a Latin verb of beating, and its senses all keep the picture of force applied at one point.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语中表示击打的动词，各个义项都保留着「在一点上使力」的画面。

normal.en: Pellere drives and pulsare beats; push is the repeated beat that finally moves the object.
normal.cn: pellere 是驱动，pulsare 是反复击打；push 就是那一下下敲击终于把东西推动了。

normal.en: Old French pousser is the direct source, which is why push looks nothing like its Latin ancestor.
normal.cn: 古法语 pousser 是直接来源，所以 push 的拼写与它的拉丁祖先毫无相似之处。

normal.en: Pushy adds -y to the action and turns it into a personality that keeps pressing other people.
normal.cn: pushy 在动作后加 -y，把「推」变成一种不断对别人施压的性格。

normal.en: A push-up is the body lifting itself by pushing down on the floor.
normal.cn: push-up 是靠向下推地面把身体撑起来的动作。

normal.en: Pushback is the force that returns when you push, now used mostly for people resisting a plan.
normal.cn: pushback 是你推出去之后返回来的一股力，如今多指人们对某项计划的抵制。

abstract.en: Force applied at one point can move a whole object, which is why the word suits hands, campaigns and markets alike.
abstract.cn: 作用在一点上的力能移动整个物体，所以这个词既能用于手，也能用于运动和推广。

abstract.en: A society moves forward when someone grows tired enough of standing still to start pushing.
abstract.cn: 社会往前动，往往是因为有人厌倦了原地不动，开始使力。

abstract.en: Pushing and pulling are the two directions of every bargain, and most deals settle somewhere between them.
abstract.cn: 推与拉是每场讨价还价的两种方向，多数交易最终落在两者之间。

examples.en: She pushed the heavy box across the floor.
examples.cn: 她把那只沉重的箱子推过地板。

examples.en: The campaign pushed hard for cleaner air.
examples.cn: 这场运动为争取更清洁的空气大力施压。

examples.en: One final push got the team over the line.
examples.cn: 最后一次发力让队伍越过了终点线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「布什」——布什总统一挥手，把前面的人往前一推，记住 push 是推。

root: 古法语 pousser（推）← 拉丁语 pulsare（反复击打）← pellere（驱动、击打）；同族有 pulse、compel、repel。

sensesIntro.en: The core is force applied at a point; the senses divide into moving an object, pressing a person, selling goods, and one organized forward effort.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是在一点上使力；义项由此分为推动物体、催逼他人、推销货物，以及一次有组织的推进。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two palms flat against a heavy door, the gap widening by a finger's width.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手掌抵住一扇沉门，门缝一点点变宽。

branches.en: a palm flat against a stuck door
branches.cn: 一只手掌平贴在卡住的门上

branches.en: a hand on someone's back at the start line
branches.cn: 起跑线上按在他人后背的手

branches.en: a new phone in every window display
branches.cn: 每个橱窗里都摆着的新手机

branches.en: a march moving one field closer
branches.cn: 向前推进一地的行军

branches.en: pressure that moves a person and a whole group
branches.cn: 推动一个人也推动一群人的力量

intro.en: The word is held together by two Latin verbs of driving and beating, an Old French verb, and English suffixes that make a person and a quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个表示驱动与击打的拉丁动词、一个古法语动词，以及构成「人」与「性质」的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: too eager to get what one wants
items.meaningCN: 过分急于得到；咄咄逼人的

definition_zh: 放；放置；表达；使处于某种状态；推迟
definition_en: to move something into a position and leave it there; to express something in words; to cause someone or something to be in a state; in put off, to delay
core_image: 一只手把杯子稳稳放到桌面上，随即松开
scene: 夜深了，母亲把洗好的碗一只只擦干，转身走向橱柜。She put the plates on the top shelf and closed the door.
sceneCN: 这里 put 是「放置」（第 1 个义项：把东西放到某处）；句意为她把盘子放到最上层架子上，然后关上柜门。画面里可留意：擦干的碗、橱柜、最上层架子。

pos.zh: 放；放置；表达；使处于；推迟

derivatives.zh: in 与 put 复合，指放进系统的内容，即输入
out 与 put 复合，指系统送出的结果，即产出
put 与 down 复合，指把人压低的话，即贬损
put 与 on 复合，指装出来的样子，即做作

senses.title: To place something somewhere
senses.definition: to move something into a position and leave it there
senses.definitionCN: 把某物移到某个位置并留在那里
senses.example: She put the keys beside the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她把钥匙放在门边。
senses.why: The earliest recorded sense is simply to set a thing down and let go, and almost every other sense grows out of that picture.
senses.whyCN: 有记录的最早义项就是把东西放下然后松手，其余义项几乎都从这幅画面长出来。

senses.title: To express something in words
senses.definition: to say or write something in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式说出或写出某事
senses.example: How should I put this so nobody is hurt?
senses.exampleCN: 这话我该怎么说才不伤人？
senses.why: Words are placed into a sentence the way objects are placed on a table, so arranging language took the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 词被安放进句子，就像东西被摆到桌面上，于是「安排语言」也用了同一个动词。

senses.title: To cause someone to be in a state
senses.definition: to cause someone or something to be in a particular situation or condition
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物进入某种处境或状态
senses.example: The new rule put everyone under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定让每个人都感到了压力。
senses.why: If a thing can be placed in a spot, a person can be placed in a condition, and the verb then means to bring that condition about.
senses.whyCN: 东西既能被放到某个位置，人也能被放进某种处境，于是这个动词就表示「使某种处境发生」。

senses.title: To delay something, in put off
senses.definition: in the phrasal verb put off, to move an event or an action to a later time
senses.definitionCN: 在短语动词 put off 中，把一件事或一个行动挪到以后
senses.example: They put off the meeting until Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把会议推迟到周五。
senses.why: Putting a thing off is putting it away from the present moment, so the spatial verb turns into a verb about time.
senses.whyCN: 把一件事推开，就是把它从当下这一刻挪走，于是空间上的动词转成了时间上的动词。

intro.en: The origin of put is uncertain. It is first recorded in Middle English, and it may come from Old English, from Old Norse pota, or from Old French bouter, all of which suggest a gesture of thrusting or placing; no reliable Latin cognate exists.
intro.cn: put 的来源不确定。它最早见于中古英语，可能来自古英语，也可能来自古诺斯语 pota 或古法语 bouter，这些说法都与「推、放」的手势有关；它没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: Old Norse pota meant to poke or thrust, and it is one of the forms often suggested as a source; the link is possible rather than proved.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 pota 意为戳、推，是常被提出的来源之一；这只是可能，并未得到确证。

items.en: Some scholars reconstruct an Old English verb putian, but it is not attested in surviving texts, so it remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 有学者为古英语重构出动词 putian，但现存文献中并无此词，所以它仍只是假说。

items.en: Old French bouter meant to thrust or shove and may have reinforced the English word, especially in southern dialects.
items.cn: 古法语 bouter 意为推、顶，可能在英格兰南部方言中加强了这个英语词。

items.en: Middle English putten is recorded from the fourteenth century with the sense of placing something somewhere.
items.cn: 中古英语 putten 自十四世纪起有记录，意为把某物放到某处。

items.en: Modern English keeps the irregular past put and builds a wide range of phrasal verbs such as put off, put up with and put forward.
items.cn: 现代英语保留不规则的过去式 put，并构成 put off、put up with、put forward 等大量短语动词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds built with put and a few words that only look similar; the near-meaning group collects other verbs of placing.
note.cn: 形近组收由 put 构成的复合词以及几个只是外形相近的词；近义组收其他表示放置的动词。

entries.definition: Data, energy or effort fed into a system.
entries.definitionCN: 输入系统的数据、能量或投入。

entries.definition: What a system produces after processing its input.
entries.definitionCN: 系统处理输入之后产生的结果。

entries.definition: A gentle stroke in golf; the word comes from Scottish and is not the verb of placing.
entries.definitionCN: 高尔夫中的轻推击球；这个词来自苏格兰语，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A soft paste used to fix glass into a frame; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 把玻璃固定到框子里的软膏；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To fix something in a particular position or spot.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物安放到特定位置。

entries.definition: To place an object carefully in a chosen spot.
entries.definitionCN: 小心地把某物放在选定的地方。

entries.definition: To spread something flat on a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物平放在表面上。

entries.definition: To arrange something deliberately for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为某个目的有意摆放某物。

normalIntro.en: The word has one unchanging past form, and its many phrasal verbs all move things in space or in time.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的过去式只有一种写法，而它的大量短语动词都在空间或时间里挪动东西。

normal.en: Put keeps the same form for the past, so only the rest of the sentence tells you when it happened.
normal.cn: put 的过去式与原型同形，只能靠句子的其余部分判断时间。

normal.en: Input and output are put with in and out: what is put in and what is put out.
normal.cn: input 与 output 就是 put 加 in 与 out：放进去的东西与送出来的东西。

normal.en: A put-down is a remark that places a person lower than they stood a moment before.
normal.cn: put-down 是一句话，把一个人放到比片刻之前更低的位置。

normal.en: Put off moves an event away from now, while put up with means to hold up under something.
normal.cn: put off 把一件事挪离当下，put up with 则是把某件事忍下来。

normal.en: Learners often master this verb last because every regular ending would sound wrong to a native ear.
normal.cn: 学习者往往最后才掌握这个动词，因为任何规则变化的词尾在本族语者听来都不对。

abstract.en: To put is to decide where a thing belongs, if only for the next minute.
abstract.cn: 放，就是决定一样东西该在哪儿，哪怕只为下一分钟。

abstract.en: Every sentence is a row of things put in order, which is why one verb serves both the table and the tongue.
abstract.cn: 每个句子都是把东西排好的一行，所以同一个动词既管桌面也管舌头。

abstract.en: Putting something off is storing it in the future, and the future is where unfinished things collect.
abstract.cn: 把事情推迟，就是把它存进未来，而未完成的事总在未来堆积。

examples.en: Please put the chairs back where you found them.
examples.cn: 请把椅子放回你原来找到的地方。

examples.en: She put her objection in the mildest words she could find.
examples.cn: 她用能找到的最温和的说法表达了反对。

examples.en: The match was put off because of the storm.
examples.cn: 比赛因暴风雨推迟了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「葡挞」——一盒葡挞往桌上一放，就记住 put 是放。

root: 中古英语 putten，可能与古诺斯语 pota（戳、推）或古法语 bouter（推）有关；没有可靠的拉丁同族词，来源一般标为不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hand setting an object down; the senses divide into placing, wording, causing a state, and moving something into the future.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一只手把物体放下；义项由此分为放置、措辞、使进入某种状态，以及把某事挪到以后。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand setting a cup firmly on a table, then letting go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把杯子稳稳放到桌面上，随即松开。

branches.en: a cup set down and released
branches.cn: 放下并松开手的杯子

branches.en: a sentence built like a shelf
branches.cn: 像架子一样搭起来的句子

branches.en: a person standing inside a new rule
branches.cn: 站在新规定里的人

branches.en: a meeting moved to another page of the calendar
branches.cn: 被挪到日历另一页的会议

branches.en: the same hand moving things in space and in time
branches.cn: 同一只手在空间与时间里挪动东西

intro.en: The word is held together by a Germanic verb of uncertain origin, a Middle English form, and English compounds that place something in or out.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个来源不确定的日耳曼语动词、一个中古英语形式，以及表示「放入、送出」的英语复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; the forms behind it are Germanic and Romance, and its origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词；它背后的形式分属日耳曼语与罗曼语，来源并不确定。

items.meaning: to place, to express, to delay
what is fed into a system
to delay to a later time

definition_zh: 拼图；谜题；难题；使困惑；苦思
definition_en: a game or problem that tests thought; something difficult to understand; to make someone confused; to think hard about something
core_image: 散落一桌的小块，拼到最后才露出完整图案
scene: 桌上摊着一张画满格子的纸，旁边散着几百块小纸板，孩子已经坐了半个下午。He could not finish the puzzle until he saw the picture on the box.
sceneCN: 这里 puzzle 是「拼图」（第 1 个义项：需要拼合图形的智力玩具）；句意为直到看见盒子上的图，他才把拼图拼完。画面里可留意：格子纸、小纸板、盒子。

pos.zh: 拼图；谜题；难题
使困惑；苦思

derivatives.zh: puzzle 加名词后缀 -ment，指被难住时的困惑状态
puzzle 加表人或表物后缀 -er，指难题，也指爱解谜的人
puzzle 与 box 复合，指要按机关才能打开的盒子

senses.title: A game made of pieces that fit together
senses.definition: a game or toy in which many small pieces must be fitted together to form a picture or a shape
senses.definitionCN: 把许多小块拼合起来、组成图案或形状的游戏或玩具
senses.example: The children spread the puzzle over the whole table.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把拼图摊满了整张桌子。
senses.why: The word first named a confusing problem, then was applied to the cut-up picture because solving one feels like rebuilding a broken whole.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指令人困惑的难题，后来用在被切成碎块的图画上，因为拼合它就像把一个破碎的整体重新装回去。

senses.title: Something difficult to understand
senses.definition: a question, situation or person that is hard to understand or explain
senses.definitionCN: 难以理解或解释的问题、局面或人
senses.example: How the thief entered the locked room remains a puzzle.
senses.exampleCN: 窃贼如何进入那间锁着的屋子仍是个谜。
senses.why: From the start the word named what stops the mind, so any event with a missing piece is called by the name of the game.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从一开始就指「卡住思路的东西」，因此任何缺了一块的事，都能用这项游戏的名字来称呼。

senses.title: To confuse someone
senses.definition: to make someone feel confused because they cannot understand something
senses.definitionCN: 使某人因为弄不明白而感到困惑
senses.example: The letter puzzled her for a long time.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信让她困惑了很久。
senses.why: If a problem is a puzzle, then meeting it is being caught inside it, so the noun turned into a verb of bafflement.
senses.whyCN: 既然难题本身是 puzzle，遇上它就像被它困在里面，于是名词转成了表示「使人为难」的动词。

senses.title: To think hard about something
senses.definition: to think long and carefully about something you cannot understand or solve
senses.definitionCN: 对无法理解或解决的事长时间仔细思考
senses.example: He puzzled over the figures until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 他对着那些数字苦思到半夜。
senses.why: The mind keeps returning to a piece it cannot place, and that repeated turning is the second life of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 心思会一次次回到那块放不下的拼图上，这种反复琢磨正是这个动词的第二重生命。

intro.en: Puzzle appears in English in the late sixteenth century, and its origin is uncertain; it may be a frequentative of pose in an older sense of perplexing someone, but no Latin cognate can be traced with confidence.
intro.cn: puzzle 在十六世纪后期出现在英语中，来源不确定；它可能是 pose 旧义「把人问住」的反复形式，但没有可确证的拉丁同族词。

items.en: The verb is first recorded as pusle, meaning to bewilder or confuse, with no earlier French or Latin form securely attached to it.
items.cn: 这个动词最早记作 pusle，意为使人迷惑，此前并没有可确证的法语或拉丁语形式与它相连。

items.en: Several explanations have been offered and none is accepted as certain, so dictionaries usually mark the origin as unknown.
items.cn: 人们提出过几种解释，但没有一种被公认，所以词典通常把来源标为不明。

items.en: One common suggestion is that the word is a frequentative of pose in the old sense to put someone to a standstill; this is generally described as possible rather than proved.
items.cn: 一种常见的说法是，它是 pose 旧义「使人僵住、问住」的反复形式；一般认为这只是可能，而非已证。

items.en: In the seventeenth century the noun named a bewildering question, and by the nineteenth century it was applied to the jigsaw picture cut into pieces.
items.cn: 十七世纪名词 puzzle 指令人困惑的问题，到十九世纪又被用在切成碎块的拼图上。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for the toy, the enigma and the act of thinking hard, and keeps puzzling as an adjective for what confuses.
items.cn: 现代英语用 puzzle 指玩具、谜团与苦思的动作，并用 puzzling 作形容词表示令人困惑的。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same stem and two words that merely rhyme; the near-meaning group collects other names for what is hard to explain.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形式，以及两个只是读音相近的词；近义组收其他表示「难以解释之物」的词。

entries.definition: Hard to understand or explain.
entries.definitionCN: 难以理解或解释的。

entries.definition: The feeling of being confused by something.
entries.definitionCN: 被某事弄糊涂的感受。

entries.definition: The nose and mouth of an animal, or a guard over them; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 动物的口鼻部，或罩在上面的套子；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To rub against something gently with the nose; only the sound is close.
entries.definitionCN: 用鼻子轻轻蹭某物；只是读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A question or statement that needs clever thought to answer.
entries.definitionCN: 需要巧思才能回答的问题或说法。

entries.definition: A person or thing that is mysterious and hard to read.
entries.definitionCN: 神秘难懂的人或事物。

entries.definition: Something that cannot be explained or is kept secret.
entries.definitionCN: 无法解释或被保密的事。

entries.definition: A network of paths designed to be hard to escape.
entries.definitionCN: 设计得难以走出的路径网。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a verb for confusing the mind, and the toy borrowed the name because it does the same thing more gently.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是一个使人脑子打结的动词，玩具借用了这个名字，只因它更温和地做着同一件事。

normal.en: The verb first meant to bewilder, and the toy took the name because a cut picture bewilders until the last piece fits.
normal.cn: 这个动词最早表示使人迷惑，玩具之所以得名，是因为在最后一块拼上之前，碎图同样让人摸不着头绪。

normal.en: Puzzlement adds -ment and names the feeling, while puzzler adds -er and names the hard question itself.
normal.cn: puzzlement 加 -ment 指那种感受，puzzler 加 -er 则指难题本身。

normal.en: Puzzling drops the final e before -ing and keeps the sense of something that confuses.
normal.cn: puzzling 在加 -ing 前去掉词尾的 e，保留「令人困惑」之意。

normal.en: Puzzle over is the pattern for thinking hard: the preposition points at the thing that will not fit.
normal.cn: puzzle over 是苦思的固定搭配：介词指向那块怎么也放不进去的东西。

normal.en: Jigsaw puzzle is a compound from the saw that once cut the picture, though few speakers now think of the tool.

abstract.en: Some questions are puzzles and some are merely painful, and treating the second as the first is a common mistake.

examples.en: Her silence puzzled everyone at the table.

definition_en: a skill, certificate or condition that makes someone suitable, or a limitation added to a statement
core_image: 在一张表上逐格打钩，够格的人才被放进候选名单
scene: 这份工作要求有教师资格，还要至少两年的课堂教学经验。The job requires a teaching qualification and at least two years of classroom experience.
sceneCN: 这里 qualification 是「资格证书」（第 2 个义项：证明具备任教资历的正式凭证）；句意：这份工作要求具备教师资格证书，以及至少两年的课堂经验。图中可辨识物件：盖章的证书、勾选过的条件清单；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Being fit for a role
senses.definition: the skills, knowledge or experience that make a person suitable for a job or role
senses.definitionCN: 使人适合某项工作或角色的技能、知识或经验
senses.example: Her qualifications for the post include six years of field research.
senses.exampleCN: 她胜任这一职位的资历包括六年实地研究经验。
senses.why: Qualis asked 'of what kind' and facere meant 'make'. To qualify is to make someone of the right kind for a role, and the noun names that fitness.
senses.whyCN: qualis 问“何种”，facere 意为“使”。qualify 就是使人变成适合某角色的那种类型，名词命名的正是这种适合。

senses.title: A certificate that proves it
senses.definition: an official certificate, degree or licence showing that a person has met a standard
senses.definitionCN: 证明某人达到某项标准的正式证书、学位或执照
senses.example: The clinic hires only nurses with a recognised qualification.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所只聘用持有认可资格证书的护士。
senses.why: The abstract fitness became a paper object: the certificate stands in for the training so an employer can check it quickly.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的适合变成一张纸：证书代替培训过程，让雇主能快速核查。

senses.title: A limit on a claim
senses.definition: a condition or limitation attached to a statement, making it narrower or less absolute
senses.definitionCN: 附加在陈述上的条件或限制，使其范围更窄或不再绝对
senses.example: He accepted the plan with one qualification: the budget must not exceed ten million.
senses.exampleCN: 他接受这项计划，但有一个限定条件：预算不得超过一千万。
senses.why: Qualis asks 'of what kind'. Here the kind is narrowed: the acceptance is not absolute but of one specific, limited kind, and the clause states the limit.
senses.whyCN: qualis 问“何种”。这里种类被收窄：接受不是绝对的，而是某个特定、有限的种类，而那个从句说明了限度。

senses.title: The act of becoming fit
senses.definition: the process of training or being certified as suitable for a profession
senses.definitionCN: 为胜任某一职业而接受培训或被认证的过程
senses.example: Qualification as a midwife takes three years in that country.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个国家，取得助产士资格需要三年。
senses.why: The noun also names the journey rather than the endpoint: the training, examinations and supervised practice that produce a qualified person.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也命名过程而非终点：产生合格者的培训、考试与督导实习。

senses.title: Grammar: narrowing a noun
senses.definition: the act of a word or phrase limiting or describing another word
senses.definitionCN: 词或短语限制、描述另一词的作用
senses.example: In 'the red door', 'red' performs a qualification of 'door'.
senses.exampleCN: 在“那扇红门”中，“红”对“门”起限定修饰作用。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the limiting sense: the modifier says what kind of door is meant, cutting the noun down from all doors to one described kind.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了限制义：修饰语说明指的是哪一种门，把名词从所有门收窄到被描述的那一种。

senses.title: A round before the main event
senses.definition: a preliminary stage in which competitors earn the right to enter the main competition
senses.definitionCN: 参赛者争取进入正赛资格的预赛阶段
senses.example: She finished second in the qualification and reached the final.
senses.exampleCN: 她在预选赛中名列第二，进入了决赛。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the fitness idea: a qualification round decides who is fit to enter the main draw.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了“适合”的观念：预选赛决定谁有资格进入正赛。

senses.title: Agreement with reservations
senses.definition: approval given with stated doubts or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在说明疑虑或条件的前提下给予赞同
senses.example: The committee gave its qualification rather than outright support.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会给出的是有保留的认可，而非无条件支持。
senses.why: Approval is granted, but as a qualified kind: the doubts are stated at the same time, so the support is real yet bounded.
senses.whyCN: 认可被给予了，但属于带限定的一类：疑虑同时被说明，因此支持是真的，却有边界。

senses.title: A restricting clause in law
senses.definition: a clause that limits the scope of a right, rule or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 限制某项权利、规则或协议范围的条款
senses.example: The lease contains a qualification on subletting the premises.
senses.exampleCN: 租约中有一条关于转租房屋的限制条款。
senses.why: Law states the limits explicitly: the clause makes the tenant's right a particular, restricted kind rather than an unrestricted one.
senses.whyCN: 法律把限度明说出来：这条使租客的权利成为某种特定、受限的类型，而非不受限制的类型。

intro.en: Qualification comes from Medieval Latin qualificatio, built on qualificare, 'to make of a certain kind'. Qualis meant 'of what kind' and facere meant 'to make'. The word began in scholastic philosophy as the assigning of a quality and later became the everyday word for fitness, certificates and reservations.
intro.cn: qualification 来自中古拉丁 qualificatio，建于 qualificare“使成为某种”之上。qualis 意为“何种”，facere 意为“使”。这个词始于经院哲学中“赋予性质”的用法，后来成为表示适合、证书与保留意见的日常词。

items.en: Qualis was the interrogative and relative word for 'of what kind'. It is the partner of quantus 'how much', and the pair still organizes scientific vocabulary.
items.cn: qualis 是表示“何种”的疑问与关系词，与 quantus“多少”配对，这对搭配至今组织着科学词汇。

items.en: Facere meant 'to make, to do'. Added to a stem, -ficare built verbs of making, as in aedificare and modificare.
items.cn: facere 意为“做、造”。加在词干后，-ficare 构成表示“使……”的动词，如 aedificare、modificare。

items.en: Scholastic Latin formed qualificare, 'to make of a certain quality or kind'. It was used for describing and for assigning properties.
items.cn: 经院拉丁语造出 qualificare“使具有某种性质或种类”，用于描述与赋予属性。

items.en: The noun qualificatio named the act of assigning a quality, and English took it up in the 15th century.
items.cn: 名词 qualificatio 命名赋予性质的行为，英语在 15 世纪吸收了它。

items.en: Legal and professional usage gave the word its two modern poles: being fit for an office, and adding a limiting condition to a claim.
items.cn: 法律与职业用法赋予这个词两个现代极点：适合某一职位，以及给陈述加上限制条件。

items.en: Public examinations made the certificate sense dominant, and sport adopted qualification for the preliminary round.
items.cn: 公共考试使证书义成为主流，体育则用 qualification 指预赛轮。

note.en: The look-alike group separates qualification from qualify, qualified and the quantity word quantification, which has a different root. The meaning group compares credentials, conditions and restrictions.
note.cn: 形近组区分 qualification 与 qualify、qualified，以及词根不同的 quantification；词义组比较资历凭证、条件与限制。

entries.definition: to become fit, to make someone fit, or to limit a statement. It is the action behind every sense of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 取得资格、使合格，或限定陈述。它是名词各义项背后的动作。

entries.definition: having the needed training, or stated with reservations. It describes the person or the approval.
entries.definitionCN: 具备所需训练，或有保留地表述的。它描述人或认可。

entries.definition: a word that limits another word, or a preliminary match. It names the limiter or the round, not the whole status.
entries.definitionCN: 限定另一词的词，或预赛。它命名限定成分或轮次，而非整体资格。

entries.definition: the act of measuring as a quantity. It looks similar but uses quantus 'how much', not qualis 'of what kind'.
entries.definitionCN: 按数量测量的行为。它看起来相似，却用 quantus“多少”，而非 qualis“何种”。

entries.definition: a qualification or document that proves trustworthiness. It is close to sense 02 but often implies proof of standing.
entries.definitionCN: 证明可信度的资格或文件。它接近第 2 义项，但常暗含地位证明。

entries.definition: the process or document of official certification. It stresses the authority that grants it.
entries.definitionCN: 官方认证的过程或文件。它强调授予认证的权威。

entries.definition: a warning or condition attached to a statement. It is the sharp word for sense 03.
entries.definitionCN: 附在陈述上的警告或条件。它是第 3 义项的锐利说法。

entries.definition: a rule that limits what may be done. It is the strongest word for sense 08.
entries.definitionCN: 限制可做之事的规则。它是第 8 义项最强的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the checklist image, then let the same word cover a certificate, a doubt, a training path, a modifier, a prelim, a reservation and a clause.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从勾选清单的画面出发，再让同一个词覆盖证书、疑虑、培训路径、修饰语、预赛、保留意见与条款。

normal.en: Split it as qual + i + fic + ation: what kind + make + noun. It names the making of a right kind of person.
normal.cn: 拆成 qual + i + fic + ation：何种、使、名词。它命名把人变成合适类型的过程。

normal.en: Picture a form with boxes to tick: only the person who fills every box enters the shortlist.
normal.cn: 想象一张打钩的表：填满每一格的人才进候选名单。

normal.en: The ticked form then becomes a certificate on the wall.
normal.cn: 这张勾好的表后来变成挂在墙上的证书。

normal.en: A qualification on a promise is a small box left unticked: agreement with one exception.
normal.cn: 承诺上的限定就是留空的一小格：同意，但有一个例外。

normal.en: A qualification round is the same shortlist, moved to a sports field.
normal.cn: 预选赛就是同一份候选名单，被搬到了运动场。

abstract.en: Hear the -fic- inside: the word is always about making someone or something fit a kind.
abstract.cn: 听见词里的 -fic-：这个词总是在讲使人或物适合某一类型。

abstract.en: Notice the two directions: outward proof (certificate) and inward limit (reservation).
abstract.cn: 注意两个方向：向外的证明（证书）与向内的限制（保留）。

abstract.en: Keep it away from quantification: one asks 'what kind', the other 'how much'.
abstract.cn: 把它与 quantification 分开：一个问“何种”，一个问“多少”。

examples.en: The fellowship lists a doctorate as a minimum qualification.
examples.cn: 这项奖学金把博士学位列为最低资格。

examples.en: She agreed to chair the panel, with the qualification that she could leave early.
examples.cn: 她同意主持专家组，但附带一个条件：她可以提前离场。

examples.en: Our team was eliminated in the qualification for the regional cup.
examples.cn: 我们队在地区杯的预选赛中被淘汰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“夸利非凯神”：夸你条件好、学历够，一张证书就神气起来。

root: 中古拉丁 qualificare“使成为某种”（qualis 何种 + facere 使）的名词 qualificatio；核心是“把人或物变成合适的类型”。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all concern fitness: the skills that fit a role, the paper that proves it, the training that produces it, the doubt that limits an agreement, the modifier that narrows a noun, the round that decides who may compete, the reservation on approval, and the clause that limits a right.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都关乎“适合”：适合某一角色的技能、证明它的纸、产生它的训练、限制协议的疑虑、收窄名词的修饰语、决定谁可参赛的轮次、认可上的保留，以及限制权利的条款。

core.en: A person or statement is narrowed to fit a standard, and the fit is then certified or limited.
core.cn: 人或陈述被收窄到符合某一标准，随后这种符合被认证或被限制。

branches.en: FITNESS: skills and a certificate show that a person suits a role.
branches.cn: 适合：技能与证书表明一个人适合某角色。

branches.en: LIMIT: agreement is narrowed by a stated condition.
branches.cn: 限制：同意被明说的条件收窄。

branches.en: PROCESS: training and examination produce the fit kind of person.
branches.cn: 过程：培训与考试产生合适类型的人。

branches.en: SCOPE: a modifier or a legal clause cuts down what the words cover.
branches.cn: 范围：修饰语或法律条款削减文字覆盖的范围。

branches.en: COMPETITION: a preliminary round decides who is fit to enter.
branches.cn: 竞争：预赛决定谁有资格进入。

intro.en: Qualification is qualis plus facere plus the noun suffix -atio. The items below follow the same making verb through verb, adjective, agent and the parallel quantity family.
intro.cn: qualification 由 qualis、facere 与名词后缀 -atio 构成。下列条目沿着同一个“使”动词，走过动词、形容词、施动者，以及平行的数量词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the kind word and the making verb. They explain why qualification, quality and qualify all turn on 'what kind'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出“何种”与“使”两个词，解释为什么 qualification、quality 与 qualify 都围绕“何种”。

items.example: The certificate is a formal qualification.
items.exampleCN: 这张证书是正式资格证明。

items.meaning: to make or become fit; to limit
items.example: Two years of practice qualify her for the licence.
items.exampleCN: 两年实践使她符合执照要求。
专家组给予了有保留的支持。

items.meaning: a limiting word; a preliminary round
items.example: In the phrase, the adjective is a qualifier.
items.exampleCN: 在该短语中，形容词是限定成分。

items.meaning: the kind or character of something
items.example: The quality of the soil improved.
The study relied on qualitative evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究依靠定性证据。

items.meaning: the loss of fitness or the act of removing it
items.exampleCN: 这次犯规导致取消资格。

items.example: Nurses complete requalification every three years.
items.exampleCN: 护士每三年完成一次资格复审。

latinEntries.meaning: a making of a certain kind

definition_zh: 使有资格；取得资格；限定；修饰；达标晋级
definition_en: to give someone the right or ability to do something; to reach the standard needed for a job or a competition; to limit the meaning of a statement; to describe or modify a word
core_image: 考场门口一张刚盖章的证书，边角还带着新墨
scene: 考场外的走廊里，她反复翻着笔记，等最后一门成绩公布。Only after passing that exam could she qualify as a nurse.
sceneCN: 这里 qualify 是「取得从业资格」（第 2 个义项：通过考核获得某种身份）；句意为只有通过那场考试，她才能取得护士资格。画面里可留意：走廊、翻旧的笔记、成绩榜。

pos.zh: 使有资格；取得资格；限定；修饰；达标晋级

derivatives.zh: qualify 去 y 加 -ication，指资格、资历或取得资格的过程
qualify 加 -ed 作形容词，指合格的、有限定条件的
qualify 加 -er，指预选赛，也指语法中起限定作用的词
dis- 与 qualify 结合，指取消某人已有的资格

senses.title: To give or have the right to something
senses.definition: to give someone the right to do or receive something, or to have that right because the conditions are met
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人做某事或获得某物的权利，或因条件满足而拥有这种权利
senses.example: Two years of residence qualify you for the local pension.
senses.exampleCN: 居住满两年就有资格领取当地的养老金。
senses.why: The medieval Latin verb meant to mark a thing with a quality, and from marking came the sense of declaring that a person meets a required standard.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语动词本指给事物标上某种性质，从「标记」引申出「声明某人达到了规定标准」。

senses.title: To train and pass the tests for a profession
senses.definition: to complete the training and pass the examinations needed to work in a profession
senses.definitionCN: 完成培训并通过从业所需的考试
senses.example: She qualified as a pharmacist in only four years.
senses.exampleCN: 她只用四年就取得了药剂师资格。
senses.why: A profession demands proof of a quality, so the verb came to name the whole process of earning that proof.
senses.whyCN: 一种职业要求证明你具备某种素质，于是这个动词就用来指取得这份证明的全过程。

senses.title: To reach the next stage of a competition
senses.definition: to reach the standard needed to continue in a competition or to enter a final stage
senses.definitionCN: 达到继续参赛或进入决赛阶段所需的标准
senses.example: Only the top two teams qualify for the final.
senses.exampleCN: 只有排名前两位的队伍才能晋级决赛。
senses.why: A league sets a line that must be crossed, and crossing that line is described with the same word as meeting any standard.
senses.whyCN: 联赛会划出一条必须越过的线，越过这条线与达到任何标准都用同一个词来描述。

senses.title: To limit or modify a word
senses.definition: to add words that limit the meaning of a statement, or in grammar to describe another word
senses.definitionCN: 加上词语以缩小某个说法的范围，或在语法上修饰另一个词
senses.example: The adverb qualifies the verb that follows it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个副词修饰它后面的动词。
senses.why: The oldest Latin sense was to assign a quality, and assigning a quality can narrow a meaning as easily as it can widen a right.
senses.whyCN: 最早的拉丁义项是「赋予某种性质」，而赋予性质既能扩大权利，也同样能缩小一个说法的范围。

intro.en: Qualify is built from Latin qualis, of what kind, and a form of facere, to make; medieval Latin qualificare meant to give a quality, and English took the word through French.
intro.cn: qualify 由拉丁语 qualis（何种的）与 facere（做）的一种形式构成；中世纪拉丁语 qualificare 意为赋予性质，英语经法语借入这个词。

items.en: Qualis was the question word for kind, meaning of what sort, and it also gave Latin qualitas, the word for a quality.
items.cn: qualis 是询问种类的疑问词，意为「何种的」，它还给出拉丁语 qualitas（性质）。

items.en: Facere meant to make or do, and it appears in a long series of Latin verbs that name the making of something.
items.cn: facere 意为做、制造，出现在一长串表示「造成某物」的拉丁动词里。

items.en: Qualificare combined the two: to assign a quality to something, and in legal use to limit or restrict a claim.
items.cn: qualificare 把两者结合：给某物标上性质；在法律用法中又指限定或缩小一项主张。

items.en: Old French qualifier carried the word into French with the sense of naming a quality and of making someone fit.
items.cn: 古法语 qualifier 把这个词带入法语，兼有「标明性质」与「使某人合格」两义。

items.en: Modern English uses the verb for rights, for professional training, for reaching a later round, and for grammar.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个动词指获得权利、完成职业训练、进入下一轮比赛，以及语法上的修饰。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same Latin stem of kind and making; the near-meaning group collects verbs of granting rights, setting standards and limiting meaning.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干（种类与制造）上的形式；近义组收表示授予权利、设定标准与限定含义的动词。

entries.definition: A certificate or skill showing that a person meets a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某人达到标准的证书或技能。

entries.definition: A match deciding who advances, or a word that limits another.
entries.definitionCN: 决定谁晋级的比赛，或限定另一词范围的词。

entries.definition: To take away someone's right to take part.
entries.definitionCN: 取消某人参加的资格。

entries.definition: A feature of a person or thing that makes it what it is.
entries.definitionCN: 使人或事物成其为自身的一种特性。

entries.definition: To state officially that someone meets a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 正式声明某人达到某个标准。

entries.definition: To give someone the right to something.
entries.definitionCN: 给予某人某项权利。

entries.definition: To change something slightly, or to limit its meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 略微改变某物，或缩小其含义。

entries.definition: To keep something within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物限制在一定范围内。

normalIntro.en: The word joins a Latin question about kind to a Latin verb of making, so its oldest idea is to give something a kind.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语中询问「何种」的词与表示制造的动词接在一起，所以它最古老的意思是「给某物一个种类」。

normal.en: Qualify joins a stem meaning of what kind with a verb meaning to make: to qualify is to give something a kind.
normal.cn: qualify 把表示「何种」的词干与表示制造的动词连起来：使合格就是给某物一个种类。

normal.en: Qualification adds -tion and names the paper or the state that proves a standard has been met.
normal.cn: qualification 加 -tion，指证明达标的那张纸或那种状态。

normal.en: Qualifier does two jobs: a team that advances, and a word that narrows another word.
normal.cn: qualifier 有两项职责：晋级的队伍，以及缩小另一词范围的词。

normal.en: Disqualify adds dis- and removes exactly the right that the base verb had granted.
normal.cn: disqualify 加 dis-，去掉的正是原动词所授予的那项权利。

normal.en: Qualify for names a benefit, while qualify as names an identity, which is why one takes for and the other takes as.
normal.cn: qualify for 指向一种待遇，qualify as 指向一种身份，所以一个用 for，一个用 as。

abstract.en: A qualification is a line drawn by others, and the verb describes both drawing it and crossing it.
abstract.cn: 资格是别人划下的一条线，而这个动词既描述划线，也描述越线。

abstract.en: Every right has a condition, and the word for meeting the condition is the same word for narrowing a claim.
abstract.cn: 每项权利都有条件，而「满足条件」与「缩小主张」用的竟是同一个词。

abstract.en: To qualify is to be judged enough by someone who has the power to decide what enough means.
abstract.cn: 取得资格，就是被某个有权定义「够」的人判定为够。

examples.en: A degree does not automatically qualify you for the job.
examples.cn: 有学位并不自动让你有资格做这份工作。

examples.en: He qualified as a lawyer last spring.
examples.cn: 他去年春天取得了律师资格。

examples.en: Please qualify your claim so that it is not read too broadly.
examples.cn: 请对你的说法加以限定，免得被理解得过宽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阔立飞」——拿到证书那一刻，身价立刻往上飞，记住 qualify 是取得资格。

root: 拉丁语 qualis（何种的）+ facere（做）→ 中世纪拉丁语 qualificare（赋予性质、限定）→ 古法语 qualifier → 英语 qualify；同族有 quality、qualification。

sensesIntro.en: The core is assigning a kind or a standard; the senses divide into granting a right, earning a professional proof, meeting a competition line, and narrowing a meaning.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是标定种类或标准；义项由此分为授予权利、取得职业证明、达到比赛门槛，以及缩小一个说法的范围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a freshly stamped certificate at an examination hall door, its ink still wet.
core.cn: 核心意象：考场门口一张刚盖章的证书，边角还带着新墨。

branches.en: a stamped form that opens a door
branches.cn: 一张盖章、能打开一扇门的表格

branches.en: a hospital corridor after the last exam
branches.cn: 最后一场考试后的医院走廊

branches.en: a finish line that leads to the final
branches.cn: 通向决赛的终点线

branches.en: an adverb narrowing a verb
branches.cn: 一个缩小动词范围的副词

branches.en: the same proof asked for in law and in training
branches.cn: 法律与训练所要的同一份证明

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin question word for kind, the verb to make, their medieval compound, and the English endings that build a noun and a negative verb.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中询问种类的疑问词、表示制造的动词、两者的中世纪复合形式，以及构成名词与否定动词的英语词缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
